words.ex: Natural science studies natural phenomena.
words.def: The branch of science that studies the natural world.

words.ex: Rain is a common natural phenomenon.
words.def: An observable event or change occurring in nature.

words.ex: A rice plant is a living thing.
words.def: An organism that can grow, reproduce, and exchange substances.

words.ex: A wooden table is a non-living thing.
words.def: An object that does not grow, reproduce, or metabolize.

words.ex: Biology is the study of living things.
words.def: The branch of science that studies living organisms.

words.ex: Chemistry studies substances and their changes.
words.def: The science of matter, substances, and chemical reactions.

words.ex: Physics studies motion, forces, and energy.
words.def: The science of matter, motion, force, and energy.

words.ex: Earth science studies the Earth and its atmosphere.
words.def: The study of the Earth, its structure, and atmosphere.

words.ex: Astronomy studies stars, planets, and space.
words.def: The scientific study of celestial bodies and the universe.

words.ex: Modern technology improves our daily life.
words.def: The application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes.

words.ex: We must follow safety rules in the laboratory.
words.def: A room equipped for scientific experiments and research.

words.ex: Always follow every safety rule during an experiment.
words.def: An instruction designed to prevent accidents or injury.

words.ex: Read the warning sign on the chemical bottle carefully.
words.def: A symbol that alerts people to potential danger.

words.ex: Keep flammable substances away from open flames.
words.def: Easily set on fire and quick to burn.

words.ex: Never taste or smell toxic chemicals in the lab.
words.def: Poisonous and harmful to health or life.

words.ex: Wear gloves when handling corrosive acids.
words.def: Capable of damaging skin, eyes, or materials on contact.

words.ex: The biohazard symbol warns of dangerous biological agents.
words.def: A biological substance that poses a threat to human health.

words.vi: nguy hiểm về điện / điện áp cao
words.ex: Do not touch wires near a high voltage sign.
words.def: Electrical energy strong enough to cause severe shock.

words.ex: Handle fragile glassware carefully so it does not break.
words.def: Easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: Wear safety goggles to protect your eyes from chemicals.
words.def: Protective eyewear worn during science experiments.

words.ex: Use a magnifying glass to observe leaf veins clearly.
words.def: A convex lens used to produce a magnified image of an object.

words.ex: A magnifying glass can magnify an image 3 to 20 times.
words.def: To make something appear larger than its actual size.

words.ex: The glass lens is thinner at the edge than in the middle.
words.def: A curved piece of transparent glass that bends light rays.

words.ex: Place the magnifying glass close to the specimen first.
words.def: A sample or small object selected for scientific observation.

words.ex: A hand lens has a frame and a handle for easy holding.
words.def: A small portable magnifying glass held in the hand.

words.ex: A desktop magnifier with a lamp helps examine fabric samples.
words.def: A stand-mounted magnifying lens often equipped with a light.

words.ex: Watchmakers use a headband magnifier to repair tiny parts.
words.def: A wearable magnifying glass fitted onto eyeglass frames or a headband.

words.ex: You can see tiny leaf veins clearly through a magnifying glass.
words.def: A vascular line running through the blade of a leaf.

words.ex: A magnifying glass makes the lines of a fingerprint easy to see.
words.def: The pattern of ridges on the tip of a human finger.

words.ex: Clean the lens regularly with a soft cloth and clean water.
words.def: To remove dirt, dust, or smudges from a surface.

words.ex: An optical microscope magnifies tiny plant and animal cells.
words.def: An instrument that uses visible light and lenses to magnify tiny objects.

words.ex: Look through the eyepiece labeled 10x to observe the specimen.
words.def: The lens at the top of a microscope that you look through.

words.ex: Select the 10x or 40x objective lens before observing.
words.def: The lens closest to the specimen on a microscope.

words.vi: đĩa quay gắn các vật kính
words.ex: Rotate the revolving nosepiece to change the objective lens.
words.def: The rotating turret that holds two or more objective lenses.

words.ex: Place the glass slide securely on the stage with clips.
words.def: The flat platform where a microscope slide is placed.

words.ex: Turn the coarse adjustment knob slowly until the specimen appears.
words.def: The large knob used for major focusing adjustments.

words.ex: Use the fine adjustment knob to bring the image into sharp focus.
words.def: The small knob used for precise, sharp focusing.

words.ex: Hold the prepared slide in place using the stage clips.
words.def: A thin flat piece of glass holding a specimen for examination.

words.ex: Hold the arm with one hand when carrying the microscope.
words.def: The curved frame connecting the head and base of a microscope.

words.ex: Support the base of the microscope with your other hand.
words.def: The bottom support structure of a microscope.

words.ex: We use a ruler to measure the length of a book.
words.def: The measurement of something from end to end.

words.ex: The meter is the standard unit of length.
words.def: The base unit of length in the SI measurement system.

words.ex: Place the ruler straight along the edge of the notebook.
words.def: A straight strip of plastic, wood, or metal used to measure length.

words.ex: Tailors use a flexible measuring tape to measure body size.
words.def: A flexible strip marked with units for measuring curved or long objects.

words.ex: A vernier caliper measures the inner and outer diameters of a pipe.
words.def: A precision instrument used to measure internal and external dimensions.

words.ex: The measuring range of this ruler is 20 centimeters.
words.def: The maximum value that a measuring instrument can measure.

words.ex: The smallest division on a standard school ruler is 1 millimeter.
words.def: The length between two consecutive scale marks on a ruler.

words.ex: Always estimate the length of an object before choosing a ruler.
words.def: To make an approximate judgment of a measurement before measuring.

words.ex: Keep your eyes perpendicular to the ruler scale when reading.
words.def: At a 90-degree angle to a given line or surface.

words.ex: A measuring cylinder helps find the volume of an irregular stone.
words.def: The amount of space that a substance or object occupies.

words.ex: A clock is a common instrument used to measure time.
words.def: The measurable period during which an action or event exists.

words.ex: The second is the base unit of time in the SI system.
words.def: The standard base unit of time, symbolized by s.

words.ex: There are sixty seconds in one minute.
words.def: A unit of time equal to 60 seconds.

words.ex: One hour equals sixty minutes or 3,600 seconds.
words.def: A period of time equal to 60 minutes.

words.ex: We use different types of clocks to measure time accurately.
words.def: A device that measures and indicates time.

words.ex: Athletes and scientists use a stopwatch to time short events.
words.def: A timepiece that can be started and stopped precisely for timing.

words.ex: A sundial tells the time by the position of a shadow in sunlight.
words.def: An ancient timekeeping device using the shadow cast by the Sun.

words.ex: An hourglass measures time as sand flows from top to bottom.
words.def: A glass device using flowing sand to measure a set period of time.

words.ex: A digital watch displays the time clearly in numbers.
words.def: A timepiece that shows the time electronically as digits.

words.ex: Always press Reset to set the stopwatch to zero before measuring.
words.def: To return a measuring device or counter to its starting zero state.

words.ex: Temperature measures how hot or cold an object is.
words.def: The degree of hotness or coldness of a body or environment.

words.ex: A thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature.
words.def: A device for measuring and indicating temperature.

words.ex: Normal human body temperature is about 37 degrees Celsius.
words.def: A unit of temperature on the Celsius scale (°C).

words.ex: On the Celsius scale, water freezes at 0°C and boils at 100°C.
words.def: A temperature scale with 0°C as freezing and 100°C as boiling.

words.ex: Liquid thermometers work based on the thermal expansion of liquids.
words.def: The increase in volume of matter in response to heating.

words.ex: Doctors use a clinical thermometer to measure body temperature.
words.def: A thermometer specifically designed to measure human body temperature.

words.ex: An infrared thermometer measures body temperature quickly without contact.
words.def: A device that infers temperature from thermal radiation.

words.ex: Mercury is a toxic liquid metal used inside some glass thermometers.
words.def: A heavy silvery toxic liquid metal used in some thermometers.

words.ex: The temperature of melting ice is 0 degrees Celsius.
words.def: Ice transitioning from solid to liquid at 0°C.

words.ex: The temperature of boiling water at standard pressure is 100°C.
words.def: Water reaching 100°C and turning into steam.

words.ex: Every object around us is made of one or more substances.
words.def: A particular kind of matter with uniform properties.

words.ex: A limestone mountain is a natural object.
words.def: A material thing that can be seen and touched.

words.ex: A lion and rubber latex are examples of natural objects.
words.def: An object formed in nature without human manufacturing.

words.ex: Long Bien Bridge and bread are artificial objects made by humans.
words.def: An object created or manufactured by human beings.

words.ex: Color, taste, and boiling point are physical properties of water.
words.def: A characteristic observed or measured without changing a substance into a new one.

words.ex: Burning coal to form carbon dioxide shows a chemical property.
words.def: The ability of a substance to undergo a change that forms a new substance.

words.ex: Water exists in three states of matter: solid, liquid, and gas.
words.def: The distinct physical form of matter: solid, liquid, or gas.

words.ex: The melting point of pure ice is 0 degrees Celsius.
words.def: The temperature at which a solid changes into a liquid.

words.ex: The boiling point of water is 100 degrees Celsius.
words.def: The temperature at which a liquid turns into vapor or gas.

words.ex: Salt and sugar both show good solubility in water.
words.def: The ability of a substance to dissolve in a liquid such as water.

words.ex: Iron and wood are substances in the solid state.
words.def: A state of matter with a fixed shape and very low compressibility.

words.ex: Water and cooking oil are examples of liquids.
words.def: A state of matter that flows easily and takes the shape of its container.

words.ex: Air inside a tire is in the gas state.
words.def: A state of matter that spreads out freely and can be compressed easily.

words.ex: Melting and boiling are common changes of state.
words.def: The physical transformation of a substance from one state of matter to another.

words.ex: Melting is the change from a solid to a liquid.
words.def: The process in which a solid turns into a liquid at its melting point.

words.ex: Freezing occurs when liquid water turns into ice at 0°C.
words.def: The process in which a liquid changes into a solid upon cooling.

words.ex: Vaporization includes both evaporation and boiling.
words.def: The process by which a liquid changes into a gas or vapor.

words.ex: Evaporation occurs at the surface of a liquid at any temperature.
words.def: Vaporization that takes place only on the surface of a liquid.

words.ex: Boiling occurs throughout the liquid at a specific boiling point.
words.def: Rapid vaporization both on the surface and inside a liquid at its boiling point.

words.ex: Clouds form through the condensation of water vapor in the sky.
words.def: The change of state from a gas or vapor into a liquid.

words.ex: Oxygen makes up about 21% of the air by volume.
words.def: A colorless, odorless gas essential for respiration and combustion.

words.ex: Nitrogen is the most abundant gas in the air at 78%.
words.def: A colorless gas making up about 78% of Earth’s atmosphere.

words.ex: Green plants absorb carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.
words.def: A gas produced by respiration and burning, used by plants in photosynthesis.

words.ex: Living organisms need oxygen for cellular respiration.
words.def: The process of breathing and releasing energy using oxygen.

words.ex: Oxygen is necessary to support combustion and burning fuel.
words.def: The chemical process of burning a fuel in the presence of oxygen.

words.ex: Smoke, dust, and toxic exhaust gases cause air pollution.
words.def: The presence of harmful substances in the air that damage health and the environment.

words.ex: Toxic factory gases react with water vapor to form acid rain.
words.def: Rain made acidic by atmospheric pollution that harms buildings, soil, and plants.

words.ex: Trees take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen during photosynthesis.
words.def: The process by which green plants make food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide.

words.ex: Water droplets on a cold test tube prove that air contains water vapor.
words.def: Water in its gaseous state present in the atmosphere.

words.ex: Solar, wind, and water power are clean energy sources.
words.def: Renewable energy that produces little or no air pollution.

words.ex: Different materials have different properties and uses.
words.def: A substance or mixture of substances from which objects are made.

words.ex: Metals conduct electricity and heat very well.
words.def: A shiny, strong material that conducts heat and electricity well.

words.ex: Plastic is lightweight, flexible, and does not conduct electricity.
words.def: A synthetic, lightweight, durable material that insulates electricity and heat.

words.ex: Glass is transparent and lets light pass through, but it is brittle.
words.def: A hard, transparent, brittle material used for bottles and windows.

words.ex: Ceramic bowls resist corrosion and conduct heat poorly.
words.def: A hard, brittle, heat-resistant material made by firing clay.

words.ex: Car tires are made of elastic and waterproof rubber.
words.def: An elastic, waterproof material that insulates heat and electricity.

words.ex: Wood is strong, easy to shape, and used to make furniture.
words.def: The hard fibrous material from trees used for building and furniture.

words.ex: Copper metal is a good electrical conductor used inside wires.
words.def: A material that allows electric current to flow through it easily.

words.vi: vật liệu cách nhiệt (dẫn nhiệt kém)
words.ex: Pot handles are made of wood or plastic as a thermal insulator.
words.def: A material that conducts heat poorly and prevents burns.

words.ex: We should reduce, reuse, and recycle waste to protect the environment.
words.def: To convert waste materials into reusable new products.

words.ex: Sugarcane is the raw material used to produce sugar.
words.def: A basic natural or artificial substance processed to make new products.

words.ex: Limestone is heated in a kiln to produce quicklime.
words.def: A sedimentary rock composed mainly of calcium carbonate.

words.ex: Quicklime is produced by roasting limestone at high temperatures.
words.def: Calcium oxide obtained by heating limestone.

words.ex: The main component of limestone is calcium carbonate.
words.def: A chemical compound found in rocks such as limestone and marble.

words.ex: Ores are rocks and soil containing valuable minerals in high amounts.
words.def: Naturally occurring rock or sediment from which metals or minerals can be extracted.

words.ex: Bauxite ore is processed to produce aluminum metal.
words.def: The primary ore used in the production of aluminum.

words.ex: Iron ore is smelted with coke to manufacture cast iron and steel.
words.def: Rock containing iron compounds from which metallic iron is extracted.

words.ex: Clay, limestone, and sand are heated to make clinker for cement.
words.def: A building binder made by heating limestone and clay.

words.ex: Natural ores are non-renewable resources that must be used wisely.
words.def: Existing in finite amounts and unable to be replaced quickly once used.

words.ex: Efficient use of raw materials supports sustainable development.
words.def: Using resources to meet present needs without harming future generations.

words.ex: Fuels are substances that burn and release a lot of heat.
words.def: A material burned to produce heat, power, or electricity.

words.ex: Coal is a solid fossil fuel mined heavily in Quang Ninh.
words.def: A black combustible sedimentary rock used as a solid fuel.

words.ex: Crude oil is refined to produce gasoline, kerosene, and fuel gas.
words.def: Unrefined liquid petroleum extracted from underground reservoirs.

words.ex: Natural gas is often found together with crude oil in oil fields.
words.def: A flammable gas found underground, used for cooking and heating.

words.ex: Gasoline is a liquid fuel used to run car and motorbike engines.
words.def: A volatile liquid fuel refined from petroleum for motor vehicles.

words.ex: Kerosene is used in oil lamps and certain heating or jet engines.
words.def: A light fuel oil distilled from petroleum.

words.ex: Coal, crude oil, and natural gas are non-renewable fossil fuels.
words.def: A natural fuel formed over millions of years from ancient organisms.

words.ex: Solar, wind, and hydro power are clean renewable energy sources.
words.def: Energy from natural sources that are constantly replenished.

words.ex: Every country needs a plan to ensure energy security for daily life and industry.
words.def: The uninterrupted availability of energy sources at an affordable price.

words.vi: tính bắt lửa / tính dễ cháy
words.ex: Gas has higher flammability than solid coal and ignites quickly.
words.def: How easily a substance catches fire and burns.

words.ex: Rice, corn, potatoes, and wheat are common staple foods.
words.def: Basic starchy foods eaten regularly as the main energy source.

words.ex: Meat, fish, eggs, and vegetables are nutritious foodstuffs.
words.def: Substances used as food to provide essential nutrients.

words.ex: Our body needs nutrients to grow, develop, and stay healthy.
words.def: A substance in food that provides nourishment essential for life and growth.

words.ex: Carbohydrates in rice and sweet potatoes provide our main energy.
words.def: A nutrient group including starch, sugar, and fiber that supplies energy.

words.ex: Starch is the main energy source found in rice, corn, and bread.
words.def: A complex carbohydrate abundant in grains and root vegetables.

words.ex: Meat, fish, eggs, milk, and beans are rich in protein.
words.def: A nutrient essential for building, maintaining, and repairing body tissues.

words.ex: Lipids in butter, vegetable oil, and peanuts store energy and keep the body warm.
words.def: Fats and oils that serve as energy reserves and help absorb certain vitamins.

words.ex: Calcium and iodine are vital minerals for strong bones and thyroid health.
words.def: Inorganic elements needed in small amounts for healthy body development.

words.ex: Fresh fruits and green vegetables provide many essential vitamins.
words.def: Organic compounds required in small quantities to regulate metabolism.

words.vi: chế độ dinh dưỡng cân đối
words.ex: Eating a balanced diet prevents malnutrition and obesity.
words.def: A diet containing proper proportions of all necessary nutrients.

words.ex: Distilled water and pure oxygen are pure substances.
words.def: Matter made of only one kind of substance with fixed properties.

words.ex: Seawater and orange juice are mixtures containing two or more substances.
words.def: A combination of two or more substances mixed together.

words.ex: Sugar water and salt water are clear, homogeneous solutions.
words.def: A homogeneous mixture of a solvent and one or more solutes.

words.ex: Water acts as the solvent when sugar dissolves in it.
words.def: The substance that dissolves a solute to form a solution.

words.ex: In salt water, salt is the solute and water is the solvent.
words.def: A substance that dissolves in a solvent.

words.ex: A solution is a homogeneous mixture with uniform appearance throughout.
words.def: A mixture in which components are evenly distributed and indistinguishable.

words.ex: Suspensions and emulsions are cloudy heterogeneous mixtures.
words.def: A mixture whose components are not evenly distributed and can be seen.

words.ex: Muddy river water is a suspension of solid particles in liquid.
words.def: A heterogeneous mixture containing solid particles suspended in a liquid.

words.ex: Milk and shaken oil-and-water mixtures are examples of emulsions.
words.def: A heterogeneous mixture of tiny liquid droplets suspended in another liquid.

words.ex: Sugar dissolves faster and in greater amounts in hot water than in cold water.
words.def: To mix completely into a liquid to form a uniform solution.

words.ex: The separation of mixtures depends on differences in physical properties.
words.def: The process of dividing a mixture into its individual components.

words.ex: Heavy mud particles sink to the bottom through sedimentation.
words.def: The settling of heavier suspended solid particles at the bottom of a liquid.

words.ex: After mud settles, clear water is poured off by decantation.
words.def: Gently pouring off a liquid from settled solid sediment.

words.ex: Filtration separates insoluble solid particles from a liquid using filter paper.
words.def: A method using a porous barrier to separate insoluble solids from liquids or gases.

words.ex: Fold the filter paper and place it inside the funnel before pouring.
words.def: Porous paper with tiny holes that traps solid particles while letting liquid pass.

words.ex: Place a funnel lined with filter paper over a glass beaker.
words.def: A cone-shaped utensil used for guiding liquid or holding filter paper.

words.ex: Evaporation to dryness recovers solid salt from salt water.
words.def: Heating a solution until all the liquid solvent evaporates, leaving solid solute.

words.ex: Extraction separates two immiscible liquids that form distinct layers.
words.def: Separating two liquids that do not dissolve in each other using a separatory funnel.

words.ex: Open the stopcock of the separatory funnel slowly to drain the lower water layer.
words.def: A laboratory funnel with a stopcock used to separate immiscible liquids.

words.ex: The clear liquid collected in the beaker after filtration is called the filtrate.
words.def: The liquid that has passed through a filter.

words.ex: All living organisms are made up of basic units called cells.
words.def: The basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms.

words.ex: Plants, animals, and humans are living organisms made of cells.
words.def: Any individual living entity such as a plant, animal, or microbe.

words.ex: Cells carry out basic life processes including growth and reproduction.
words.def: The process of increasing in size or developing over time.

words.ex: Cells can divide and reproduce to form new cells.
words.def: The biological process by which new cells or organisms are produced.

words.ex: Waste substances leave the cell through excretion.
words.def: The process of removing waste products from a cell or organism.

words.ex: Cells respond to changes in their environment.
words.def: Reacting to internal or external signals or changes.

words.ex: Cell shape often reflects the specific function of the cell.
words.def: The outer form or structure of a cell.

words.ex: Most cells have a small cell size and are seen with a microscope.
words.def: The dimensions or scale of a cell.

words.ex: A nerve cell has long branches to transmit signals.
words.def: A specialized cell that transmits nerve impulses in animals.

words.ex: A bacterial cell is usually microscopic and seen under a microscope.
words.def: A microscopic single-celled organism.

words.ex: The cell membrane surrounds the cytoplasm and controls substance exchange.
words.def: The outer boundary present in every cell that regulates exchange with the environment.

words.ex: Most metabolic activities of the cell take place in the cytoplasm.
words.def: The jelly-like region between the cell membrane and the nucleus or nucleoid.

words.ex: The nucleus contains genetic material and controls all cell activities.
words.def: The membrane-bound control center of a eukaryotic cell.

words.ex: A prokaryotic bacterial cell has a nucleoid instead of a true nucleus.
words.def: The region in a prokaryotic cell containing genetic material without a nuclear membrane.

words.ex: Genetic material is stored inside the nucleus or nucleoid.
words.def: DNA or hereditary molecules that carry instructions for cell functions.

words.ex: A bacterial cell is a prokaryotic cell lacking a nuclear membrane.
words.def: A cell without a membrane-bound nucleus or membrane-bound organelles.

words.ex: Plant and animal cells are eukaryotic cells with a true nucleus.
words.def: A complex cell containing a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles.

words.ex: The rigid cell wall protects the plant cell and maintains its shape.
words.def: A tough outer layer outside the cell membrane in plant cells.

words.ex: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll to absorb sunlight for photosynthesis.
words.def: A green organelle in plant cells where photosynthesis occurs.

words.ex: Plant cells have a large central vacuole that stores nutrients, pigments, or wastes.
words.def: A fluid-filled sac inside cells used for storage and maintaining pressure.

words.vi: sự lớn lên của tế bào
words.ex: Through metabolism, a small new cell undergoes cell growth into a mature cell.
words.def: The increase in size and mass of a newly formed cell.

words.vi: sự phân chia (sinh sản) của tế bào
words.ex: When a cell reaches a certain size, it undergoes cell division into two daughter cells.
words.def: The process by which one parent cell divides into two daughter cells.

words.ex: One parent cell divides to produce two identical daughter cells.
words.def: The original cell that divides to form new daughter cells.

words.ex: Newly formed daughter cells are small and grow larger through metabolism.
words.def: One of the two new cells formed when a parent cell divides.

words.ex: A young cell absorbs nutrients and grows into a mature cell.
words.def: A fully grown cell ready to perform its role or divide.

words.ex: Metabolism enables a young cell to increase in size and mass.
words.def: The chemical processes inside a cell that sustain life and growth.

words.ex: A corn plant and a human being are multicellular organisms made of many cells.
words.def: An organism composed of many specialized cells.

words.ex: A unicellular organism grows solely by increasing the size of its single cell.
words.def: An organism consisting of only a single cell.

words.ex: Cell division produces new cells to replace old, dead, or damaged cells.
words.def: A cell that has been injured or impaired and needs replacement.

words.ex: Uncontrolled cell division can form abnormal masses called tumors.
words.def: An abnormal mass of tissue formed when cells divide uncontrollably.

words.vi: tế bào biểu bì hành tây
words.ex: Onion epidermal cells are rectangular plant cells observed under a microscope.
words.def: A thin outer plant cell layer peeled from an onion scale for microscopic viewing.

words.ex: Fish egg cells are large enough to observe with the naked eye or a hand lens.
words.def: A large spherical animal cell visible without a high-power microscope.

words.ex: Place a drop of distilled water on a clean glass slide before mounting the sample.
words.def: A flat rectangular piece of glass on which a specimen is placed.

words.ex: Lower the coverslip gently from one edge to avoid trapping air bubbles.
words.def: A very thin square piece of glass placed over a specimen on a slide.

words.ex: Use a dropper to add a drop of distilled water onto the glass slide.
words.def: A small glass or plastic tube with a rubber bulb for dispensing liquid drops.

words.ex: Use a dissecting needle to gently peel the thin onion epidermis and separate fish eggs.
words.def: A sharp pointed tool used for manipulating delicate biological specimens.

words.ex: Place a few fish eggs and some water into a petri dish for observation.
words.def: A shallow cylindrical transparent dish used to hold samples in the lab.

words.ex: Use filter paper to absorb excess water around the edge of the coverslip.
words.def: Absorbent paper used to blot away extra liquid from a microscope slide.

words.ex: Carefully cut a small 7–8 mm square on the inner onion scale using a scalpel.
words.def: A small, sharp surgical knife used for precise cutting in biology labs.

words.vi: tiêu bản tạm thời (tiêu bản ướt)
words.ex: Prepare a wet mount of onion epidermis in distilled water before viewing at 10x and 40x.
words.def: A microscope slide preparation in which the specimen is suspended in a drop of liquid.

words.ex: An organism is an individual living thing that performs basic life processes.
words.def: An individual living entity capable of carrying out all basic life processes.

words.ex: An amoeba and a bacterium are unicellular organisms made of one cell.
words.def: An organism consisting of only a single cell that performs all life functions.

words.ex: A frog, a rabbit, and an apricot tree are multicellular organisms.
words.def: An organism made up of many specialized cells working together.

words.ex: An amoeba is a microscopic unicellular protozoan seen under a microscope.
words.def: A single-celled protozoan that changes shape and moves using pseudopods.

words.ex: Baker’s yeast is a unicellular fungus used in making bread.
words.def: A microscopic single-celled fungus.

words.ex: Nutrition is the process of taking in food and water for energy and growth.
words.def: The life process of obtaining and using food and water.

words.ex: Sensitivity allows an organism to sense and respond to changes in its environment.
words.def: The ability to detect and respond to environmental stimuli.

words.ex: Animals show movement when responding to food, danger, or changes around them.
words.def: An action or change in position or place by a living organism.

words.ex: Respiration, nutrition, growth, excretion, and reproduction are basic life processes.
words.def: An essential biological activity required to maintain life.

words.ex: Multicellular organisms have specialized cells that perform distinct functions together.
words.def: A cell adapted to carry out a specific role in a multicellular body.

words.ex: Similar cells working together form a tissue, such as muscle tissue.
words.def: A group of similar cells connected together to perform a specific function.

words.ex: The stomach, heart, and leaf are examples of organs.
words.def: A structure made of two or more tissues working together for a specific life activity.

words.ex: The digestive system and respiratory system are organ systems in humans.
words.def: A group of organs that cooperate to perform a major life process.

words.ex: The levels of organization go from cell to tissue, organ, organ system, and organism.
words.def: The hierarchical arrangement of biological structures from simple to complex.

words.ex: Epithelial tissue covers and protects the outer surface of skin, roots, stems, and leaves.
words.def: Protective tissue covering body surfaces and plant organs.

words.ex: Muscle tissue contracts and relaxes to produce movement in animals.
words.def: Animal tissue specialized for contraction and movement.

words.ex: Connective tissue supports and connects different organs in the body.

words.def: Exerting force away from oneself to move or change an object.

words.ex: Pulling a wagon or stretching a rubber band applies a pull force.
words.def: Exerting force toward oneself to move or stretch an object.

words.ex: A force can make a moving object speed up, slow down, start moving, or stop.
words.def: Making an object move faster, slower, start from rest, or stop.

words.ex: A defender’s kick deflects a moving soccer ball to the left, changing its direction.
words.def: Altering the path or direction in which an object moves.

words.ex: Compressing a spring or stretching a rubber band changes its shape—called deformation.
words.def: A change in the shape of an object caused by an applied force.

words.ex: A contact force occurs when the object applying the force touches the object receiving it.
words.def: A force exerted when the acting object physically touches the affected object.

words.ex: A non-contact force acts even without physical contact, such as a magnet or gravity.
words.def: A force exerted without physical touch between objects, such as magnetic or gravitational force.

words.vi: lò xo lá tròn và xe lăn
words.ex: In Experiment 1 (Figure 40.4), a compressed leaf spring pushes a roller cart when released.
words.def: Apparatus in Experiment 1 testing contact push from a spring on a cart.

words.vi: tương tác xe lăn gắn nam châm
words.ex: In Experiment 2 (Figure 40.5), magnet force acts on cart A even before cart B touches it.
words.def: Apparatus in Experiment 2 demonstrating non-contact magnetic force.

words.ex: Magnitude is the strength of a force; pushing a stalled car is stronger than pressing a bell.
words.def: How strong a force is, measured in newtons (N).

words.ex: The unit of force in Vietnam’s legal measurement system is the newton, symbolized by N.
words.def: The standard unit of force, named after Isaac Newton, symbolized by N.

words.ex: A force meter measures force magnitude; set it to zero before pulling along the force line.
words.def: An instrument (such as a spring scale) used to measure force in newtons.

words.ex: In tug-of-war, two teams pull along a horizontal line in opposite directions (left vs. right).
words.def: The straight line (direction/line) and sense (left/right, up/down) along which a force acts.

words.ex: The tail/origin of the force arrow is placed at the point of application on the object acted on.
words.def: The location on an object where a force is applied, at the arrow’s tail.

words.ex: A force arrow shows point of application, line and direction, and magnitude to scale.
words.def: An arrow drawn to represent a force’s point of application, direction, and magnitude.

words.vi: tỉ xích biểu diễn độ lớn lực
words.ex: At scale 1 cm = 10 N, a 30 N horizontal push to the right is drawn as a 3 cm arrow.
words.def: The ratio relating arrow length (cm) to force magnitude (N).

words.vi: lực của dây câu tác dụng lên con cá
words.ex: In Figure 41.5a, the fishing line pulls the fish upward along a vertical line.
words.def: Upward vertical pull exerted by the fishing line on the fish.

words.vi: lực của tay kéo dây cung
words.ex: In Figure 41.5b, the archer pulls the bowstring horizontally to the left.
words.def: Horizontal pull exerted on the bowstring when drawing a bow.

words.vi: lực của vận động viên lên ván nhảy
words.ex: In Figure 41.5c, the diver pushes downward along a vertical line on the diving board.
words.def: Downward vertical push exerted by a diver on a diving board.

words.ex: A coil spring stretches or compresses under force and returns to original shape when force stops.
words.def: Change in length/shape of a spring under force, recovering when force is removed.

words.vi: độ dãn của lò xo (Δl = l - l0)
words.ex: Extension Δl equals stretched length l minus initial length l0.
words.def: Increase in spring length: Δl = l - l0.

words.vi: chiều dài ban đầu của lò xo (l0)
words.ex: Measure initial length l0 of the hanging spring before hanging weights.
words.def: Original length of an unstretched spring.

words.vi: chiều dài của lò xo khi bị dãn (l)
words.ex: Measure length l when a weight is hung from the spring.
words.def: Total length of a spring while stretched by a hanging mass.

words.vi: lực đàn hồi của lò xo
words.ex: When you pull a spring, the spring pulls back on your hand with an elastic force.
words.def: Restoring force exerted by a deformed spring or elastic object.

words.ex: Steel and brass have good elasticity, whereas aluminum and lead have poor elasticity.
words.def: Ability of a material/spring to return to its original shape after force is removed.

words.vi: giới hạn đo (GHĐ) của lực kế / cân lò xo
words.ex: Stretching a spring past its measuring limit can permanently deform it and ruin elasticity.
words.def: Maximum load/force a spring scale can measure without losing elasticity.

words.ex: Motorcycle shock absorbers use spring deformation to smooth bumps.
words.def: Device using springs to cushion shocks and vibrations on vehicles.

words.ex: Trampolines use springs around the frame to stretch and bounce.
words.def: Bouncing mat supported by springs that deform and rebound.

words.ex: Clothespins grip using spring deformation.
words.def: Clip using a small spring to clamp objects.

words.ex: Any two objects with mass attract each other; this attraction is called gravitational force.
words.def: Attractive force between any two objects that possess mass.

words.ex: A released apple or object falls downward because of Earth’s gravitational pull.
words.def: Gravitational attraction exerted by Earth on objects.

words.ex: Weight P is the magnitude of Earth’s gravitational pull on an object, measured in newtons (N).
words.def: Magnitude of Earth’s gravitational force on an object, denoted P and measured in N.

words.ex: Mass measures the amount of matter in an object in kg and does not change between Earth and Moon.
words.def: Measure of amount of matter in kg, measured with a balance.

words.vi: phương thẳng đứng, chiều từ trên xuống dưới
words.ex: Falling objects show that Earth’s pull acts vertically downward from top to bottom.
words.def: Direction of Earth’s gravitational pull as shown by falling objects.

words.vi: lực hấp dẫn trên Mặt Trăng
words.ex: On the Moon, a 1 kg object experiences about 1.7 N pull compared with 9.8 N on Earth.
words.def: Gravitational attraction on the Moon, about one-sixth of Earth’s.

words.vi: lực hấp dẫn trên Hỏa tinh
words.ex: On Mars, a 1 kg object experiences about 3.6 N gravitational pull (Table 43.1).
words.def: Gravitational attraction on Mars (~3.6 N per kg in Table 43.1).

words.vi: nhà du hành vũ trụ trên Mặt Trăng
words.ex: Astronauts move easily on the Moon despite a 50 kg suit because Moon gravity is weaker.
words.def: Space travelers moving on the Moon under weaker gravitational pull.

words.vi: Isaac Newton và ý tưởng lực hấp dẫn
words.ex: Seeing a ripe apple fall inspired Newton’s ideas on gravity and gravitational attraction.
words.def: Scientist who developed laws of motion and gravity after observing falling objects.

words.ex: Weight P in newtons is approximately 10 times mass m in kilograms.
words.def: Approximate relation: weight in N is about 10 times mass in kg.

words.ex: Friction is a contact force appearing at the contact surface between two objects.
words.def: A contact force arising at the interface between two touching surfaces.

words.ex: Static friction keeps an object stationary even when pushed or pulled.
words.def: Friction that prevents a stationary object from moving when a push or pull is applied.

words.ex: Sliding friction occurs when one object slides across the surface of another.
words.def: Friction acting when one surface slides over another surface.

words.ex: Magnified views of wood and tabletops show roughness that causes friction between touching surfaces.
words.def: Microscopic unevenness of surfaces that produces friction when in contact.

words.ex: Ball bearings fitted on rotating axles reduce friction by replacing sliding with rolling.
words.def: Bearing with metal balls used on axles to reduce friction.

words.ex: Sliding friction between a sliding block and table opposes motion and slows the block down.
words.def: Acting against an object’s motion or push.

words.ex: Friction between the ground and a walker’s foot pushes the walker forward.
words.def: Helping an object or person move forward.

words.vi: khía rãnh trên mặt lốp xe
words.ex: Grooves on car and motorbike tires increase grip/friction and drain water for road safety.
words.def: Tread patterns on tires that improve traction and safety, especially on wet roads.

words.ex: Walking on a wet slippery floor or riding on worn bald tires risks slipping and skidding.
words.def: Losing traction and sliding unintentionally on a surface.

words.ex: When braking hard, friction acts on the wheels/tires and slows or stops the bicycle/car.
words.def: Slowing or stopping a vehicle using brakes and road-tire friction.

words.ex: Objects moving through water experience a drag force from the water.
words.def: Resistive force exerted by water on an object moving through it.

words.ex: In Figure 45.1, a rectangular barrier plate attached to the cart moves through water.
words.def: Plate attached to the test cart to experience drag force in water.

words.ex: Larger obstacle area in water produces a stronger water drag force.
words.def: Surface area facing the flow/motion; larger area means greater drag.

words.vi: hình khí động học / thuôn gọn
words.ex: Aquatic animals like sharks, swordfish, and tuna have streamlined shapes to reduce water drag.
words.def: Smooth, tapered body shape that reduces fluid resistance during movement.

words.ex: Air also exerts drag on moving objects, stronger when frontal area is larger.
words.def: Resistive force exerted by air on objects moving through it.

words.ex: A fixed pulley in Figure 45.1 guides the string so pulling downward on the force meter pulls the cart.
words.def: Pulley mounted in a fixed position to redirect the pulling string.

words.ex: Item 9 in Figure 45.1 is the water drain valve at the bottom of the tank.
words.def: Valve used to drain water from the experimental tank.

words.vi: vận động viên đua xe đạp cúi người
words.ex: Crouching low and wearing an aerodynamic helmet reduces air drag so cyclists go faster.
words.def: Lowering posture and using streamlined gear to reduce air resistance.

words.ex: Submarines move much slower than airplanes largely because water drag is much greater than air drag.
words.def: Comparison showing higher fluid resistance in water than in air.

words.ex: The force meter reads higher when water is in the tank because it must overcome water drag too.
words.def: Value shown on the 5 N spring force meter during steady cart motion.

words.ex: Every natural phenomenon needs energy; we sense energy through its effects.
words.def: Capacity to exert force or drive changes/phenomena; measured in joules (J).

words.ex: The unit of energy is the joule (J), named after James Prescott Joule (1818–1889).
words.def: Standard unit of energy (J); 1 kJ = 1,000 J, 1 cal ≈ 4.2 J.

words.ex: Materials like gasoline, oil, coal, wood, and waste that release energy, heat, and light when burned are fuels.
words.def: Material that releases energy, producing heat and light when burned.

words.vi: truyền năng lượng qua tác dụng lực
words.ex: Wind transfers energy to turn a pinwheel or wind turbine blades by exerting a force.
words.def: Transferring energy from one object to another through force action.

words.vi: truyền năng lượng qua truyền nhiệt
words.ex: Energy transfers from a stove to a kettle of water by heating, raising its temperature.
words.def: Transferring thermal energy from a warmer source to another object.

words.ex: Light wind spins a pinwheel; strong wind spins wind turbine blades.
words.def: Devices moved by wind energy transferred through force.

words.ex: Strong prolonged wind or tornadoes can exert destructive forces on buildings.
words.def: Powerful rotating wind capable of exerting strong destructive forces.

words.vi: thổi xe đồ chơi qua ống hút
words.ex: Blowing harder through a straw transfers more energy, making the toy car move faster and farther.
words.def: Classroom activity in Figure 46.2 linking energy to force and travel distance.

words.vi: năng lượng dự trữ trong pin
words.ex: Stored energy in a flashlight or phone battery powers light, sound, and images.
words.def: Energy stored in batteries used to run lights and electronic devices.

words.vi: năng lượng ánh sáng Mặt Trời
words.ex: Plants absorb sunlight energy to grow, flower, and bear fruit.
words.def: Energy from sunlight driving plant growth and natural processes.

words.ex: Any moving object has kinetic energy, such as a spinning fan blade, blowing wind, or rolling ball.
words.def: Energy possessed by an object because of its motion.

words.ex: Objects elevated above the ground store gravitational potential energy, like water in a hydro dam.
words.def: Energy stored due to an object’s height/position above the ground.

words.ex: Chemical energy is stored in food, batteries, candles, matches, and fireworks and released in reactions.
words.def: Energy stored in chemical substances and released during chemical reactions.

words.ex: Electrical energy comes from power plants, batteries, solar cells, or hydro and runs appliances.
words.def: Energy associated with electric current from generators, batteries, or power grids.

words.ex: Light energy radiates from the Sun, lamps, or light-emitting organisms like fireflies.
words.def: Energy emitted by light sources such as the Sun or lamps.

words.ex: Sound energy travels from vibrating sources like bells, speakers, guitar strings, and voices.
words.def: Energy carried by sound waves from vibrating sources.

words.ex: Thermal energy comes from heat sources like the Sun, gas stoves, incandescent bulbs, and burning fuels.
words.def: Heat energy radiated or generated by warm/burning sources.

words.vi: nước chứa trong hồ thủy điện
words.ex: Water held high in a hydroelectric reservoir stores gravitational potential energy.
words.def: Elevated water storing potential energy in a dam reservoir.

words.ex: Fireworks and matches store chemical energy released as light, sound, and heat.
words.def: Examples storing chemical energy released during chemical reactions.

words.vi: sự rung động của màng loa
words.ex: Touching a TV speaker or water near a speaker reveals sound energy through vibration.
words.def: Observable vibration caused by sound energy.

words.ex: Energy changes from one form into another, such as potential to kinetic and vice versa.
words.def: Converting energy from one form to another.

words.vi: định luật bảo toàn năng lượng
words.ex: Energy is neither created nor destroyed; it only transforms or transfers between objects.
words.def: Law stating energy is never created or destroyed, only transformed or transferred.

words.vi: được bảo toàn / năng lượng toàn phần
words.ex: Total energy of a ball is conserved and never disappears or is created from nothing.
words.def: Remaining constant in total amount during transformations and transfers.

words.vi: quả bóng rổ nảy lên, rơi xuống
words.ex: Rising ball converts kinetic to potential; falling ball converts potential to kinetic energy.
words.def: Example in Figure 48.1 showing energy transformation and bounce loss to heat/sound.

words.vi: sơ đồ dòng năng lượng máy sấy tóc
words.ex: A hair dryer converts electrical energy into kinetic energy (fan), thermal energy (heating coil), and sound.
words.def: Energy conversion in a hair dryer shown in Figure 48.3.

words.vi: xoa hai bàn tay vào nhau
words.ex: Rubbing hands together warms them because motion/mechanical energy converts to thermal energy.
words.def: Everyday example of thermal energy generated by rubbing.

words.vi: thí nghiệm hai con lắc va chạm
words.ex: Pulling ball (2) to B and releasing transfers motion to ball (1) toward A.
words.def: Experiment in Figure 48.5 demonstrating energy transfer and conservation.

words.ex: Pushing a swing occasionally keeps it reaching initial height despite energy going to heat/sound/air.
words.def: Example in Figure 48.6 showing why periodic push is needed.

words.vi: thí nghiệm quả bóng tennis nảy
words.ex: A tennis ball dropped from 1 m bounces lower than 1 m because part becomes heat and sound.
words.def: Experiment in Figure 48.7 showing why rebound height is less than drop height.

words.ex: Twisting a rubber band stores elastic energy that rolls the spool when released.
words.def: DIY toy in Figure 48.4 demonstrating stored energy driving motion.

words.ex: Useful energy is the part of energy serving the intended purpose, such as heating water in a kettle.
words.def: Energy converted into the desired form for a specific purpose.

words.ex: Wasted energy always appears during energy conversion and often takes the form of thermal energy.
words.def: Energy not serving the intended purpose, often appearing as heat, sound, or unwanted light.

words.ex: In Figure 49.3, a 100 J incandescent bulb gives only 5 J visible light and 95 J heat.
words.def: Traditional filament lamp with high heat waste (95 J out of 100 J).

words.ex: In Figure 49.3, a 100 J compact lamp gives 20 J visible light and 80 J heat.
words.def: Energy-saving fluorescent bulb with 20 J visible light out of 100 J.

words.ex: In Figure 49.3, a 100 J LED lamp gives 80 J visible light and only 20 J heat.
words.def: High-efficiency lamp converting 80 J of 100 J electrical energy into visible light.

words.ex: Boiling water with an electric kettle wastes less energy than an open firewood or coal stove.
words.def: Electrical water boiler with lower energy waste than open wood/coal fires.

words.ex: Open wood or coal stoves lose substantial heat to surroundings during boiling.
words.def: Traditional solid-fuel stoves with higher heat loss to air.

words.vi: năng lượng hao phí khi ô tô chạy
words.ex: Cars running on fuel produce wasted thermal and sound energy that affects the environment.
words.def: Unwanted heat and noise released when a car runs.

words.vi: sơ đồ hiển thị năng lượng
words.ex: Diagrams in Figures 49.2 and 49.3 show input energy splitting into useful and wasted parts.
words.def: Visual chart showing input energy and useful vs. wasted output energies.

words.ex: LED lamps have much higher lighting efficiency than incandescent or compact bulbs.
words.def: Effectiveness of converting electrical energy into visible light rather than heat.

words.ex: Renewable energy is naturally available and continuously replenished, such as solar, wind, and water.
words.def: Energy naturally available and continuously replenished by natural processes.

words.ex: Non-renewable energy takes millions to hundreds of millions of years to form and will run out.
words.def: Energy sources taking millions of years to form that cannot be quickly replenished.

words.ex: Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity, and solar heaters warm water above 60°C.
words.def: Energy from the Sun, practically inexhaustible in daily use.

words.ex: Wind energy is a clean renewable energy source available in nature.
words.def: Renewable energy obtained from moving air/wind.

words.ex: Water energy comes from flowing water, tides, or ocean waves.
words.def: Energy from flowing water, tides, or waves.

words.ex: Geothermal energy comes from heat inside Earth’s core, hot springs, or geysers.
words.def: Heat energy from inside the Earth.

words.ex: Biomass energy comes from plants, wood, straw, waste, and organic matter.
words.def: Energy obtained from plants, wood, straw, waste, and biomass.

words.ex: Biofuel can be produced from agricultural/plant materials and organic waste using solar-driven growth.
words.def: Fuel produced from biological/plant materials and organic waste.

words.vi: nhiên liệu hóa thạch (than đá, dầu mỏ, khí tự nhiên)
words.ex: Coal, oil, and natural gas are non-renewable and cause more harm than renewables.
words.def: Finite fossil fuels taking millions of years to form.

words.vi: rác thải pin mặt trời đã qua sử dụng
words.ex: Scientists warn that improperly handled spent solar panels can create hazardous chemical waste.
words.def: Environmental concern noted in "Em có biết?" regarding spent solar panels.

words.ex: Energy saving cuts costs, conserves non-renewable energy, and reduces waste and pollution.
words.def: Using energy wisely to lower costs, conserve non-renewable resources, and cut pollution.

words.vi: rút phích cắm hoặc tắt thiết bị khi không dùng
words.ex: Turning off or unplugging unused electrical devices prevents energy waste.
words.def: Switching off or unplugging idle appliances to avoid unnecessary power use.

words.ex: Using natural daylight instead of electric lamps during daytime saves electricity.
words.def: Daytime sunlight used for illumination instead of artificial lights.

words.vi: phơi quần áo dưới nắng thay vì dùng máy sấy
words.ex: Drying wet clothes in sunlight instead of a clothes dryer saves energy.
words.def: Using solar heat to dry clothes rather than an electric dryer.

words.vi: tái sử dụng và tái chế
words.ex: Reusing or recycling paper, plastic, and cardboard boxes reduces waste and saves energy.
words.def: Using items again or reprocessing waste materials like boxes into useful items.

words.vi: sản phẩm tái chế từ hộp giấy (mô hình, đồ chơi, túi giấy)
words.ex: Figure 51.1 shows toys, models, storage boxes, and paper bags made from cardboard boxes.
words.def: Useful items crafted from discarded cardboard boxes.

words.vi: bóng sợi đốt và bóng compact
words.ex: Table 51.2 compares a 75 W incandescent bulb (1,000 h, 5,000 VND) and a 20 W compact bulb (5,000 h, 40,000 VND).
words.def: Two bulb types compared over 1 year (365 days × 12 h/day = 4,380 h) at 1,500 VND/kWh.

words.vi: cạn kiệt nguồn không tái tạo và ô nhiễm
words.ex: Non-renewable fuels are running out and burning them causes air pollution and climate issues.
words.def: Exhaustion of finite fuels and environmental harm from burning them.

words.ex: A school environmental ambassador proposes projects to conserve energy and protect the environment.
words.def: Student role promoting energy conservation and environmental protection.

words.vi: tắt vòi nước khi đánh răng / tiết kiệm nước
words.ex: Turning off the tap while brushing teeth saves water and energy used to pump/treat water.
words.def: Avoiding wasted running water during daily hygiene.

words.ex: The Sun appears to move from east to west across the sky because Earth rotates west to east.
words.def: Motion perceived by an observer due to the observer’s own real motion.

words.ex: Earth rotating around its axis from west to east in ~24 hours is the real motion.
words.def: Actual physical motion of an object, such as Earth’s rotation on its axis.

words.vi: sự tự quay của Trái Đất từ tây sang đông
words.ex: Earth spins once around its axis in 24 hours (one day–night cycle) from west to east.
words.def: Spinning of Earth on its axis from west to east over ~24 hours.

words.ex: Celestial bodies are natural objects in space, including stars, planets, moons, and comets.
words.def: Any natural object existing in outer space.

words.ex: A star is a celestial body that emits its own light, such as the Sun.
words.def: A self-luminous celestial body, such as the Sun.

words.ex: A planet does not emit its own light, orbits a star, and is seen by reflected starlight.
words.def: A non-luminous body orbiting a star and visible by reflected light.

words.ex: A natural satellite does not emit its own light, orbits a planet, and reflects starlight.
words.def: A non-luminous body orbiting a planet, such as the Moon around Earth.

words.ex: Comets are made mainly of frozen gases and cosmic dust and have a tail-like shape.
words.def: A small icy/dusty body with a comet-like tail shape rather than a sphere.

words.vi: chòm sao (ví dụ: Gấu Lớn / Bắc Đẩu)
words.ex: A constellation is a group of stars forming a recognizable geometric pattern, like the Big Dipper.
words.def: A pattern or group of stars connected by imaginary lines into a geometric shape.

words.ex: Ancient people used sundials with a pointer angled by local latitude to tell daytime time.
words.def: An ancient timekeeping device using shadow position cast by sunlight.

words.vi: Mặt Trăng (vệ tinh tự nhiên của Trái Đất)
words.ex: The Moon is Earth’s only natural satellite and shines by reflecting sunlight.
words.def: Earth’s sole natural satellite, visible because it reflects sunlight.

words.vi: các pha của Mặt Trăng / hình dạng nhìn thấy
words.ex: The visible shape of the Moon changes through the lunar cycle as positions change.
words.def: Changing illuminated shapes of the Moon seen from Earth over a lunar month.

words.ex: At new Moon (position 1), the sunlit side of the Moon faces away from Earth so none is seen.
words.def: Phase when no sunlit part of the Moon is visible from Earth.

words.ex: Crescent phases appear between new Moon and quarter Moon and between quarter and new Moon.
words.def: Curved/crescent illuminated shape of the Moon seen in part of the lunar cycle.

words.ex: Quarter Moon (positions 3 and 7) shows half of the illuminated face of the Moon.
words.def: Phase showing half of the Moon’s visible disk illuminated (around days 8 and 23).

words.ex: At full Moon (position 5, ~day 16 in Fig. 53.2), the entire sunlit face is seen from Earth.
words.def: Phase when the entire sunlit side facing Earth appears as a full circle.

words.vi: Tuần Trăng / chu kì pha Mặt Trăng (29,5 ngày)
words.ex: The apparent cycle of Moon phases (lunar cycle) is about 29.5 days.
words.def: Cycle of Moon phases (~29.5 days); full Moons are about 4 weeks apart.

words.vi: phản chiếu ánh sáng Mặt Trời
words.ex: We see the Moon because its sunlit side reflects sunlight toward Earth.
words.def: Sunlight bouncing off the Moon’s surface toward observers on Earth.

words.vi: một phía luôn hướng về Trái Đất
words.ex: Because Moon’s rotation and orbit periods match, one side always faces Earth.
words.def: Phenomenon where only one face of the Moon is seen from Earth.

words.vi: mô hình quan sát các pha Mặt Trăng
words.ex: A hanging ball in a cardboard chamber lit by a flashlight models Moon phases from peepholes.
words.def: Lab model using a ball, flashlight, and peepholes to observe Moon phases.

words.ex: The Solar System consists of the Sun, eight planets, dwarf planets, moons, comets, asteroids, meteoroids, and dust.
words.def: The Sun and all celestial bodies orbiting it, including eight planets.

words.ex: 1 AU equals the average distance from Earth to the Sun, about 150 million km.
words.def: Astronomy distance unit equal to Earth–Sun distance (~150 million km).

words.ex: Mercury is closest to the Sun (0.39 AU) with an 88-day orbital period around the Sun.
words.def: Closest planet to the Sun (0.39 AU; orbit 88 days).

words.ex: Venus is at 0.72 AU with a 224.7-day orbit and a 244-day rotation period.
words.def: Second inner planet from the Sun (0.72 AU; orbit 224.7 days).

words.ex: Earth is at 1 AU from the Sun with a 1-day rotation and 365.2-day orbital period.
words.def: Third planet from the Sun at 1 AU (~150 million km).

words.ex: Mars is at 1.52 AU with a 1.03-day rotation and 687-day orbital period.
words.def: Fourth inner planet from the Sun (1.52 AU; day ~1.03 Earth days).

words.ex: Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars are inner rocky/silicate-metal planets inside the main asteroid belt.
words.def: Four inner planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars) made mostly of silicates and metals.

words.vi: các hành tinh vòng ngoài (khí khổng lồ)
words.ex: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune are large outer gas planets far from the Sun with lower temperatures.
words.def: Four outer planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune) with large size and lower temperatures.

words.ex: Neptune is farthest from the Sun at 30.07 AU with a 60,152-day orbital period.
words.def: Farthest planet from the Sun (30.07 AU; orbit 60,152 days).

words.ex: The main asteroid belt lies outside the four inner rocky planets in the Solar System.
words.def: Region of asteroids separating inner planets from outer planets.

words.ex: The Milky Way is a spiral galaxy of hundreds of billions of celestial bodies bound by gravity.
words.def: A spiral galaxy of hundreds of billions of celestial bodies including our Solar System.

words.vi: vòng xoắn (cánh tay xoắn của Ngân Hà)
words.ex: Viewed perpendicular from above, the Milky Way has a spiral shape with 4 main spiral arms.
words.def: Spiral structures of the Milky Way; the Solar System lies near the edge of one arm.

words.ex: A light-year is the distance light travels in one year (~95 trillion km); Milky Way diameter is ~100,000 ly.
words.def: Astronomical distance traveled by light in 1 year (~95 trillion km).

words.ex: Our Solar System lies near the edge of a spiral arm, about 26,000 light-years from the galactic center.
words.def: Central region of the Milky Way, ~26,000 light-years from the Solar System.

words.vi: 230 triệu năm (chu kì quanh tâm Ngân Hà)
words.ex: Even at ~220,000 m/s, the Sun takes about 230 million years to complete one orbit around the Milky Way center.
words.def: Time taken by the Sun to orbit once around the center of the Milky Way.

words.ex: Beyond the Milky Way, the universe contains trillions of other galaxies of various shapes.
words.def: A vast system of stars, gas, dust, and celestial bodies bound by gravity.

words.vi: đài thiên văn (trạm quan sát thiên văn)
words.ex: Observatories house telescopes and instruments to observe and study celestial objects in the sky.
words.def: Facility equipped with telescopes and instruments for astronomical observation.

words.vi: Đài thiên văn Hòa Lạc và Nha Trang (VNSC)
words.ex: Vietnam has observatories under VNSC, including Nha Trang (completed Aug 2017) and Hoa Lac.
words.def: Astronomical observatories of the Vietnam National Space Center (VNSC).

words.vi: Galileo quan sát sao riêng biệt trong Ngân Hà (1610)
words.ex: In 1610, Galileo was the first to observe individual stars within the Milky Way band.
words.def: Astronomer who first observed separate stars in the Milky Way in 1610.

words.vi: mô hình giấy Ngân Hà quay
words.ex: A paper pinwheel painted with a spiral Milky Way models how the galaxy spins in space.
words.def: Hands-on model in Figure 55.2 illustrating a rotating spiral galaxy.

words.vi: phương pháp tìm hiểu tự nhiên
words.ex: Natural inquiry uses scientific evidence to investigate phenomena in nature and daily life.
words.def: A systematic method of investigating natural phenomena and proving ideas with evidence.

words.ex: Forming a scientific prediction helps answer the research question before testing.
words.def: Stating what may happen or be true based on observation, knowledge, and reasoning.

words.ex: Observation uses senses and instruments to gather data about shapes, sizes, and changes.
words.def: Using senses or measuring tools to collect information about objects and phenomena.

words.ex: Classification groups objects or events into categories based on chosen features.
words.def: Grouping items, concepts, or events according to selected characteristics.

words.ex: Linking observations and prior knowledge reveals relationships among natural phenomena.
words.def: Using data and existing knowledge to identify new relationships between phenomena.

words.ex: Measurement requires choosing instruments with suitable range and smallest division.
words.def: Determining quantities such as mass, length, or time using appropriate instruments.

words.ex: A photogate acts as a switch controlling a digital timer using infrared light.
words.def: An optical sensor with transmitter and receiver that triggers a digital timer.

words.vi: đồng hồ đo thời gian hiện số
words.ex: Set the digital timer to mode A<->B to measure time between photogates A and B.
words.def: An electronic timer controlled by photogates to measure short time intervals.

words.ex: Select a timer range of 99.99 s with 0.01 s resolution when measuring up to tens of seconds.
words.def: The maximum value that a measuring instrument can measure.

words.ex: A lab report includes purpose, materials, procedure, results, and answers to questions.
words.def: A structured written or presented record of an experiment or investigation.

words.ex: All natural and artificial matter is made of tiny particles called atoms.
words.def: The basic tiny particle that makes up all substances.

words.ex: The atomic nucleus lies at the center and contains protons and neutrons.
words.def: The positively charged central core of an atom made of protons and neutrons.

words.ex: Each proton carries one unit of positive electric charge (+1).
words.def: A positively charged (+1) subatomic particle in the nucleus.

words.ex: A neutron has no electric charge and has a mass of about 1 amu.
words.def: An electrically neutral subatomic particle found in the nucleus.

words.ex: Electrons are negatively charged (-1) and move in shells around the nucleus.
words.def: A negatively charged (-1) particle moving in shells around the nucleus.

words.ex: The first inner electron shell holds up to 2 electrons; the second holds up to 8.
words.def: An energy level or orbit in which electrons move around the nucleus.

words.vi: đơn vị khối lượng nguyên tử (amu)
words.ex: Atomic mass is measured in amu, with one proton or neutron about 1 amu.
words.def: The unit of atomic mass equal to one-twelfth of a carbon atom’s mass.

words.vi: số đơn vị điện tích hạt nhân (Z)
words.ex: The nuclear charge number Z equals the total number of protons in the nucleus.
words.def: The number of protons in an atom’s nucleus, denoted by Z.

words.ex: An atom is electrically neutral because proton count equals electron count.
words.def: Having equal positive and negative charges so net charge is zero.

words.vi: mô hình nguyên tử Rutherford – Bohr
words.ex: In the Rutherford–Bohr model, electrons move in shells around a central nucleus.
words.def: The atomic model showing electrons arranged in shells around a positive nucleus.

words.ex: A chemical element consists of atoms with the same number of protons.
words.def: A pure species of atoms having the same proton number (atomic number).

words.ex: The atomic number equals the number of protons in the nucleus.
words.def: The number of protons in an atom’s nucleus, unique to each element.

words.ex: Each chemical element has a global symbol of one or two letters.
words.def: A standardized letter symbol representing a chemical element worldwide.

words.vi: Liên minh Quốc tế về Hóa học cơ bản và Ứng dụng
words.ex: Element names are standardized globally according to IUPAC rules.
words.def: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry.

words.ex: Hydrogen has atomic number 1, symbol H, and atomic mass ~1 amu.
words.def: Element 1 with symbol H and atomic mass ~1 amu.

words.ex: Carbon has atomic number 6, symbol C, and atomic mass ~12 amu.
words.def: Element 6 with symbol C and atomic mass ~12 amu.

words.ex: Nitrogen has atomic number 7, symbol N, and atomic mass ~14 amu.
words.def: Element 7 with symbol N and atomic mass ~14 amu.

words.ex: Oxygen has atomic number 8, symbol O, and makes up 65% of human body mass.
words.def: Element 8 with symbol O and atomic mass ~16 amu.

words.ex: Sodium has symbol Na from its Latin name natrium and atomic mass ~23 amu.
words.def: Element 11 with symbol Na (from Latin natrium) and mass ~23 amu.

words.ex: Potassium has symbol K from its Latin name kalium and atomic mass ~39 amu.
words.def: Element 19 with symbol K (from Latin kalium) and mass ~39 amu.

words.vi: bảng tuần hoàn các nguyên tố hóa học
words.ex: The periodic table arranges 118 elements into cells, periods, and groups.
words.def: A chart organizing chemical elements by increasing nuclear charge, periods, and groups.

words.ex: Each element cell shows atomic number, symbol, name, and atomic mass.
words.def: A single box in the periodic table displaying data for one element.

words.ex: Elements in the same period have the same number of electron shells.
words.def: A horizontal row of elements with the same number of electron shells (1 to 7).

words.ex: Elements in the same group A have the same number of outer electrons (except He).
words.def: A vertical column of elements with similar chemical properties.

words.ex: Most of the 118 elements are metals, located in the lower-left and group B/bottom rows.
words.def: Elements that typically lose electrons to form positive ions and conduct electricity/heat.

words.ex: Nonmetals are mostly in the upper-right of the periodic table, such as O, S, Cl, and Br.
words.def: Elements mostly in the upper-right that tend to gain electrons to form negative ions.

words.ex: Noble gases in group VIIIA have stable outer electron shells and rarely react.
words.def: Stable elements in group VIIIA with 8 outer electrons (2 for He).

words.ex: Group VIIA is called the halogens and includes fluorine, chlorine, and bromine.
words.def: The group VIIA elements containing typical nonmetals.

words.ex: Group IA is the alkali metal group (except hydrogen).
words.def: The group IA elements (except H), which are typical metals.

words.ex: In 1869, Mendeleev arranged known elements by atomic mass and discovered periodicity.
words.def: Russian chemist (1834–1907) who developed an early periodic table in 1869.

words.ex: A simple substance is made of only one chemical element, such as copper or oxygen.
words.def: A substance composed of only one chemical element.

words.ex: A compound is made of two or more chemical elements, such as water or salt.
words.def: A substance formed from two or more different chemical elements.

words.ex: A molecule is the representative particle of a substance with its chemical properties.
words.def: A particle made of bonded atoms that represents a substance’s chemical properties.

words.ex: Molecular mass in amu is the sum of the atomic masses of atoms in the molecule.
words.def: The total mass of all atoms in a molecule, measured in amu.

words.ex: Water, carbon dioxide, table salt, and calcium carbonate are inorganic compounds.
words.def: A compound such as water, salt, or carbon dioxide (typically without carbon–hydrogen chains).

words.ex: Glucose, sucrose, and proteins are examples of organic compounds.
words.def: Compounds such as glucose, sucrose, and proteins found in living organisms.

words.ex: Ozone is a simple substance made solely of oxygen atoms.
words.def: A substance formed from oxygen atoms (O3).

words.ex: Diamond and graphite are different simple forms made only of carbon.
words.def: Different forms of a simple substance made solely of carbon.

words.ex: A methane molecule consists of one carbon atom bonded to four hydrogen atoms.
words.def: A compound molecule containing one carbon and four hydrogen atoms (CH4).

words.ex: Fuels often contain hydrocarbons made of carbon and hydrogen.
words.def: A compound composed of carbon and hydrogen.

words.ex: Atoms form chemical bonds to achieve a stable noble-gas outer electron shell.
words.def: An attraction or shared electron pair that holds atoms or ions together.

words.ex: An atom becomes a charged ion when it loses or gains electrons.
words.def: A charged particle formed when a neutral atom loses or gains electrons.

words.ex: Metal atoms tend to lose electrons to form positive ions such as Na+ and Mg2+.
words.def: A positively charged ion formed by losing one or more electrons.

words.ex: Nonmetal atoms tend to gain electrons to form negative ions such as Cl- and O2-.
words.def: A negatively charged ion formed by gaining one or more electrons.

words.ex: An ionic bond is formed by attraction between oppositely charged ions.
words.def: A bond formed by electrostatic attraction between positive and negative ions.

words.ex: Ionic compounds like table salt are solid, hard to vaporize, and conduct electricity in solution.
words.def: A compound held together by ionic bonds, such as NaCl.

words.ex: A covalent bond is formed by sharing one or more pairs of electrons between atoms.
words.def: A chemical bond formed by sharing one or more electron pairs between atoms.

words.ex: Water, oxygen, ammonia, and carbon dioxide are covalent substances.
words.def: A substance whose atoms are held together by covalent bonds.

words.ex: Two hydrogen atoms share one electron pair to form an H2 molecule.
words.def: A pair of electrons shared between two bonded atoms.

words.ex: Helium is inert and non-flammable, so it safely fills balloons instead of hydrogen.
words.def: Chemically stable and unreactive under normal conditions.

words.ex: A chemical formula represents a substance using element symbols and subscripts.
words.def: A notation of element symbols with lower-right subscripts showing composition and mass.

words.vi: chỉ số (ở chân bên phải kí hiệu)
words.ex: Subscripts show the number of each atom in a molecule; subscript 1 is omitted.
words.def: A small number written at the lower right of a symbol indicating atom count.

words.ex: Valence indicates an atom’s bonding capacity; H is assigned I and O is II.
words.def: A number expressing the combining or bonding capacity of an atom or group.

words.ex: In a two-element compound AxBy, x × valence(A) = y × valence(B).
words.def: For AxBy, the product of subscript and valence of A equals that of B.

words.vi: phần trăm khối lượng nguyên tố
words.ex: Element mass percentage equals (atomic mass × atom count ÷ molecular mass) × 100%.
words.def: The percentage of total molecular mass contributed by a specific element.

words.ex: Groups such as OH, NO3, SO4, CO3, and PO4 have their own valences in compounds.
words.def: A group of bonded atoms that acts as a unit with a specific valence in formulas.

words.ex: In H2SO4, the SO4 group is bonded to two H atoms and has valence II.
words.def: A common acid with formula H2SO4 where SO4 has valence II.

words.ex: CaCO3 has 1 Ca, 1 C, and 3 O atoms, with molecular mass 100 amu.
words.def: Compound of Ca, C, and O with molecular mass 40 + 12 + 48 = 100 amu.

words.ex: KNO3 is a fertilizer with molecular mass 39 + 14 + 48 = 101 amu.
words.def: Compound of K, N, and O with molecular mass 101 amu.

words.ex: In SO2, sulfur has valence IV since it bonds with two oxygen atoms of valence II.
words.def: Compound of S and O where S has valence IV and O has valence II.

words.ex: Speed measures how fast or slow an object moves: v = s / t.
words.def: Distance traveled per unit time, given by v = s / t.

words.ex: Distance traveled s divided by time t gives the speed of motion.
words.def: The length of the path covered by a moving object, denoted by s.

words.ex: Time interval t is the duration taken to travel distance s.
words.def: The elapsed time required to travel a distance, denoted by t.

words.ex: Meter per second (m/s) is an official unit of speed in Vietnam.
words.def: A standard SI-derived unit of speed equal to meters divided by seconds.

words.ex: 1 m/s equals 3.6 km/h, and 1 km/h equals 1/3.6 m/s.
words.def: A common unit of speed equal to kilometers traveled per hour.

words.ex: In real life, object speed often changes, so v = s / t is called average speed.
words.def: The overall speed calculated from total distance over total time.

words.ex: A cheetah can run up to about 120 km/h, much faster than a human sprinter.
words.def: A fast land animal capable of reaching speeds up to ~120 km/h.

words.ex: A snail moves slowly at about 5 × 10^-3 km/h.
words.def: A slow-moving animal with a speed around 5 × 10^-3 km/h.

words.ex: In Table 8.2, a person walking has a speed of about 1.5 m/s.
words.def: A person traveling on foot, with typical speed around 1.5 m/s.

words.ex: In Table 8.2, a commercial airplane has a speed around 200 m/s.
words.def: A passenger aircraft moving at roughly 200 m/s.

words.ex: A stopwatch measures travel time between start and finish lines in lab experiments.
words.def: A timing instrument used to measure elapsed time in experiments and sports.

words.ex: A speedometer displays the speed of vehicles such as cars and motorbikes.
words.def: An instrument on a vehicle that indicates its speed.

words.ex: Measure distance s and start timing as the object crosses the start line.
words.def: The marked starting position where motion or timing begins.

words.ex: Stop timing when the moving object reaches the finish line.
words.def: The marked end position of the measured path.

words.ex: Speed cameras time vehicles between road markers to check speed limits and reduce accidents.
words.def: Traffic monitoring equipment used to measure vehicle speeds on roads.

words.ex: In Figure 9.3, an electromagnet holds the steel ball until released.
words.def: A magnet controlled by electric current, used to hold or release a steel ball.

words.ex: The steel ball rolls down the track past photogates 3 and 4.
words.def: A metal sphere used as the moving object in the photogate speed experiment.

words.vi: Hệ thống định vị toàn cầu (GPS)
words.ex: Smartwatches and phones with GPS track position changes to compute speed.
words.def: Global Positioning System used by devices to track location, distance, and speed.

words.ex: A wooden board propped on books forms a ramp for a toy car in Figure 9.2.
words.def: A sloped surface used to guide motion in speed experiments.

words.ex: Repeat the measurement 3 times and find average distance and time before computing v.
words.def: The mean of repeated measurements taken to improve reliability.

words.vi: đồ thị quãng đường – thời gian (s–t)
words.ex: A distance–time graph shows how distance traveled changes with time.
words.def: A graph plotting distance s against time t to describe motion.

words.ex: The vertical axis Os represents distance traveled using a suitable scale.
words.def: The upright axis Os on an s–t graph representing distance s.

words.ex: The horizontal axis Ot represents time using a suitable scale.
words.def: The horizontal axis Ot on an s–t graph representing time t.

words.ex: Point O represents the starting point where time t = 0 and distance s = 0.
words.def: The starting point (0, 0) where initial time and distance are zero.

words.ex: A slanted straight line on an s–t graph shows motion with constant speed.
words.def: An inclined linear segment on an s–t graph indicating steady speed.

words.vi: đoạn thẳng song song trục thời gian
words.ex: A horizontal segment parallel to the time axis means the object is stopped.
words.def: A flat segment parallel to the t-axis showing zero distance change (stationary).

words.ex: In the first 3 hours, distance is directly proportional to time (60 km/h).
words.def: Increasing or decreasing together in the same ratio.

words.ex: From hour 3 to hour 4 (180 km to 180 km), the bus is stopped for rest.
words.def: Not moving; remaining at the same position over time.

words.vi: bảng ghi quãng đường theo thời gian
words.ex: First make a table of distance versus time before plotting the graph.
words.def: A table recording distance values at corresponding time intervals.

words.ex: Choose a suitable scale on the s and t axes so all points fit clearly.
words.def: The proportion used to represent real distances and times on graph axes.

words.ex: Obeying speed limits and safe distances keeps road users safe.
words.def: Practices and rules that protect drivers, passengers, and pedestrians on roads.

words.ex: On highways without rain, the speed sign shows a maximum speed of 120 km/h.
words.def: The highest legal speed permitted for a vehicle on a road section.
