k6l14.raw: Fossil fuels are non-renewable resources that take millions of years to form.
k6l14.hint: How long do fossil fuels take to form?
k6l14.expl: Coal, crude oil, and natural gas took millions of years to form and are non-renewable.

k6l15.q: Which nutrient group is the main source of energy for the human body?

a.quiz: Carbohydrates

k6l15.hint: Found abundantly in rice, corn, potatoes, and sugar.
k6l15.expl: Carbohydrates (starch and sugar) are digested into glucose and broken down to release the main energy for the body.

k6l15.q: Which foods are especially rich in protein for building and developing the body?
opts: Meat, fish, eggs, milk, and beans

a.quiz: Meat, fish, eggs, milk, and beans

k6l15.hint: Think of animal products and legumes.
k6l15.expl: Meat, fish, eggs, milk, and beans/lentils are major sources of protein.

k6l15.q: What health problem can occur when the body lacks calcium or vitamin D?
opts: Weak, porous bones and poor growth

a.quiz: Weak, porous bones and poor growth

k6l15.hint: Calcium and vitamin D are essential for the skeleton.
k6l15.expl: Calcium builds strong bones and vitamin D helps calcium absorption; lacking them leads to weak bones and stunted growth.

k6l15.q: Why should carrots and tomatoes be cooked with a little oil or fat?
opts: To change their color to blue
Because vitamin A is fat-soluble and needs oil or fat to be absorbed

a.quiz: Because vitamin A is fat-soluble and needs oil or fat to be absorbed

k6l15.hint: Vitamin A belongs to the fat-soluble vitamin group (A, D, E, K).
k6l15.expl: Vitamin A dissolves in fats/oils; eating carrots or tomatoes with cooking oil helps the body absorb vitamin A effectively.

k6l15.q: Why is it dangerous to eat moldy rice or moldy peanuts?
opts: They produce extremely toxic substances that can cause liver cancer
They contain too much vitamin C

a.quiz: They produce extremely toxic substances that can cause liver cancer

k6l15.hint: Mold in hot, humid conditions generates dangerous toxins.
k6l15.expl: In hot, humid weather, moldy rice and peanuts produce deadly toxins (such as aflatoxin) that can cause cancer.

k6l15.q: ___ in rice, corn, and potatoes is the main energy source for our body.

a.quiz: Starch

k6l15.sentence: Starch is the main energy source for our body.
k6l15.hint: Think of the main carbohydrate in staple foods.
k6l15.expl: Starch is a carbohydrate abundant in rice, corn, and potatoes that supplies the body’s primary energy.

k6l15.q: A lack of ___ in the diet can cause thyroid disorders such as goiter.

a.quiz: iodine

k6l15.hint: This mineral is often added to table salt.
k6l15.expl: Iodine deficiency leads to thyroid gland enlargement (goiter).

k6l15.q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence.
k6l15.raw: Carbohydrates are the main source of energy for the human body.
k6l15.sentence: Carbohydrates are the main source of energy for the human body.
k6l15.expl: This states the primary function of carbohydrates.
Vitamin C is water-soluble, whereas vitamins A, D, and E are fat-soluble.

k6l15.q: Eating too much food with very little physical activity causes excess energy to be stored as body fat.
k6l15.hint: Think about energy balance and nutrition.
k6l15.expl: When energy intake exceeds physical expenditure, the body stores the surplus as fat (lipids).

k6l15.q: Find and correct the mistake: Proteins are the main energy source, while carbohydrates are only needed in tiny amounts like vitamins.

a.fix: Carbohydrates are the main energy source, while vitamins and minerals are needed in small amounts.

k6l15.raw: Carbohydrates are the main energy source, while vitamins and minerals are needed in small amounts.
k6l15.hint: Check the roles of carbohydrates vs. vitamins.
k6l15.expl: Carbohydrates supply the main energy; proteins build the body; vitamins and minerals are needed in small quantities.

k6l16.q: Which of the following is an example of a pure substance?

a.quiz: Distilled water for injection

k6l16.hint: A pure substance contains only one kind of substance.
k6l16.expl: Distilled water consists solely of water, whereas seawater, orange juice, and sugar water are mixtures.

k6l16.q: In a cup of salt water, what are the solvent and the solute?
opts: Salt is the solvent; water is the solute
Water is the solvent; salt is the solute
Both salt and water are solvents
Neither salt nor water is a solute

a.quiz: Water is the solvent; salt is the solute

k6l16.hint: The liquid that does the dissolving is the solvent.
k6l16.expl: Water dissolves the salt, so water is the solvent and salt is the solute.

k6l16.q: What is a heterogeneous mixture of solid particles floating in a liquid called?

a.quiz: Suspension

k6l16.hint: Think of muddy river water or arrowroot powder in water.
k6l16.expl: A suspension consists of solid particles suspended throughout a liquid, such as muddy water.

k6l16.q: Which of the following is an example of an emulsion?
opts: Milk or shaken oil and water

a.quiz: Milk or shaken oil and water

k6l16.hint: An emulsion consists of liquid droplets dispersed in another liquid.
k6l16.expl: Milk and oil-in-water mixtures are emulsions (liquid-in-liquid heterogeneous mixtures).

k6l16.q: How does increasing water temperature affect the solubility of solids and gases?
opts: Both solids and gases dissolve more
Solids dissolve more and faster, while gases dissolve less
Solids dissolve less, while gases dissolve more
Temperature has no effect on solubility

a.quiz: Solids dissolve more and faster, while gases dissolve less

k6l16.hint: Compare dissolving sugar in hot tea versus opening a warm soda.
k6l16.expl: Higher temperatures increase the solubility and dissolving rate of most solids, while decreasing the solubility of gases.

k6l16.q: A ___ is a homogeneous mixture of a solvent and a solute.

a.quiz: solution

k6l16.sentence: A solution is a homogeneous mixture of a solvent and a solute.
k6l16.hint: Think of clear sugar water or vinegar.
k6l16.expl: A solution has solute particles evenly distributed in the solvent, forming a clear homogeneous mixture.

k6l16.q: Stirring, crushing into fine powder, and heating the water help solid sugar ___ faster.

a.quiz: dissolve

k6l16.hint: How do you make sugar disappear quickly in water?
k6l16.expl: Heating, stirring, and grinding a solid into smaller grains speed up the dissolving process.

k6l16.q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence.
k6l16.raw: A pure substance consists of only one substance and has fixed properties.
k6l16.sentence: A pure substance consists of only one substance and has fixed properties.

k6l16.expl: Distilled water is a pure substance, while seawater, orange juice, and milk are mixtures.

k6l16.q: Carbon dioxide gas is dissolved under pressure in carbonated soft drinks and bubbles out when the bottle is opened.
k6l16.hint: Think about opening a bottle of soda.
k6l16.expl: Gases like carbon dioxide can dissolve in water under pressure and escape as bubbles when opened.

k6l16.q: Find and correct the mistake: An emulsion consists of solid particles suspended in a liquid, like muddy water.

a.fix: A suspension consists of solid particles suspended in a liquid, while an emulsion consists of liquid droplets in another liquid.

k6l16.raw: A suspension consists of solid particles suspended in a liquid, while an emulsion consists of liquid droplets in another liquid.
k6l16.hint: Distinguish between solid-in-liquid and liquid-in-liquid mixtures.
k6l16.expl: Suspensions have solid particles in liquid (muddy water); emulsions have liquid droplets in liquid (milk, oil and water).

k6l17.q: Which method is best for separating insoluble soil particles from muddy water?
opts: Filtration using filter paper and a funnel

a.quiz: Filtration using filter paper and a funnel

k6l17.hint: Soil particles are solid and do not dissolve in water.
k6l17.expl: Filtration traps larger insoluble soil particles on the filter paper while allowing clear water (filtrate) to pass through.

k6l17.q: How is table salt obtained from seawater in salt fields or the laboratory?
opts: By evaporation to dryness using sunlight, wind, or heat

a.quiz: By evaporation to dryness using sunlight, wind, or heat

k6l17.hint: Water evaporates while salt stays behind as a solid.
k6l17.expl: Evaporation to dryness removes the volatile water solvent, leaving solid salt crystals behind.

k6l17.q: Which piece of equipment is used to separate cooking oil from water?

a.quiz: Separatory funnel

k6l17.hint: Oil and water form two separate liquid layers.
k6l17.expl: Oil and water are immiscible liquids; a separatory funnel lets you drain the denser bottom water layer first.

k6l17.q: In a separatory funnel containing cooking oil and water, which liquid settles at the bottom layer?
opts: Cooking oil, because it is heavier
Water, because it is denser than cooking oil
Both mix into a single clear layer
Neither liquid stays in the funnel

a.quiz: Water, because it is denser than cooking oil

k6l17.hint: Cooking oil floats on top of water.
k6l17.expl: Water has a higher density than cooking oil, so water forms the lower layer and drains out first when the stopcock is opened.

k6l17.q: How can you separate a dry mixture of table salt and sand?
opts: Pass a magnet over the mixture
Dissolve in water, filter out the sand, then evaporate the salt solution to dryness
Pour directly into a separatory funnel
Let the mixture sit in a dark room

a.quiz: Dissolve in water, filter out the sand, then evaporate the salt solution to dryness

k6l17.hint: Salt dissolves in water, whereas sand does not.
k6l17.expl: Adding water dissolves salt; filtration removes insoluble sand; evaporation to dryness recovers pure solid salt.

k6l17.q: ___ separates insoluble solid particles from a liquid using a funnel and filter paper.

a.quiz: Filtration

k6l17.sentence: Filtration separates insoluble solids from a liquid.
k6l17.hint: Think about the tiny pores in filter paper.
k6l17.expl: Filtration uses porous filter paper to trap solid particles while letting liquid pass through.

k6l17.q: To separate cooking oil and water, pour the mixture into a ___ and let it form two layers.

a.quiz: separatory funnel

k6l17.hint: This glassware has a stopcock at the bottom.
k6l17.expl: A separatory funnel separates two immiscible liquids that form distinct layers.

k6l17.q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence.
k6l17.raw: Substances in a mixture are separated based on their different physical properties.
k6l17.sentence: Substances in a mixture are separated based on their different physical properties.
k6l17.expl: This states the core principle of separating mixtures.

k6l17.hint: Three items are methods for separating mixtures.
k6l17.expl: Photosynthesis is a biological process in plants, not a mixture separation method.

k6l17.q: When using a separatory funnel, open the stopcock slowly so the two liquid layers do not remix.
k6l17.hint: Think about controlling the flow of the lower layer.
k6l17.expl: Opening the stopcock slowly prevents turbulence and allows you to close it right when the interface reaches the valve.

k6l17.q: Find and correct the mistake: Dissolved salt can be separated from salt water by pouring it through ordinary filter paper.

a.fix: Dissolved salt can be separated from salt water by evaporation to dryness.

k6l17.raw: Dissolved salt can be separated from salt water by evaporation to dryness.
k6l17.hint: Are dissolved salt particles trapped by filter paper?
k6l17.expl: Dissolved salt particles are too tiny for filter paper; evaporation to dryness removes the water and leaves solid salt.

k6l18.q: Why is the cell considered the basic unit of life?
opts: Because cells are larger than whales
Because all living organisms are made of cells and cells perform basic life processes
Because cells never change or reproduce

a.quiz: Because all living organisms are made of cells and cells perform basic life processes

k6l18.hint: Think about structure and life functions.
k6l18.expl: All living organisms are built from cells, and each cell can perform basic life processes such as growth, nutrition, respiration, and reproduction.

k6l18.q: Which statement about cell shape and size is correct?
opts: All cells have the exact same shape and size
All cells have the same shape but different sizes
Different types of cells usually have different shapes and sizes
All cells have the same size but different shapes

a.quiz: Different types of cells usually have different shapes and sizes

k6l18.hint: Compare skin cells, nerve cells, and plant leaf cells.
k6l18.expl: Cell shape often matches cell function, and cell size varies across organisms and organs.

k6l18.q: Which of the following is a basic life process carried out by a cell?

a.quiz: Growth, respiration, and reproduction

k6l18.expl: Cells grow, take in nutrients, respire, respond to stimuli, excrete waste, and reproduce.

k6l18.q: Which cells generally require a microscope to be seen clearly?

a.quiz: Bacterial, plant, and animal cells

k6l18.hint: Check the size scale from nanometers to kilometers.
k6l18.expl: Bacteria, plant cells, and animal cells are microscopic and observed using microscopes, whereas large organisms are visible to the naked eye.

k6l18.q: Who first observed and named "cells" in cork tissue using a simple microscope in 1665?

a.quiz: Robert Hooke

k6l18.expl: In 1665, English scientist Robert Hooke observed small box-like structures in cork and called them "cells".

k6l18.q: All living organisms are built from ___, which are the basic units of life.

a.quiz: cells

k6l18.sentence: All living organisms are built from cells.
k6l18.hint: Compare a house made of bricks with an organism made of...
k6l18.expl: Just as a house is built from bricks, living organisms are made of cells.

k6l18.q: The ___ of different cells often reflects their specialized functions.

a.quiz: shapes

k6l18.hint: Think about a branching nerve cell versus a flat skin cell.
k6l18.expl: Different shapes help cells perform specific roles in an organism.

k6l18.q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence.
k6l18.raw: Most cells are very small and can only be observed with a microscope.
k6l18.sentence: Most cells are very small and can only be observed with a microscope.

k6l18.hint: Three items are types of cells or organisms with cells.
k6l18.expl: A brick is a non-living building material, not a cell.

k6l18.q: Most cells are very small because substances must enter and leave efficiently across the cell surface.
k6l18.hint: Think about nutrients, oxygen, and waste moving across the surface.
k6l18.expl: A small size helps exchange of raw materials and wastes keep up with life processes.

k6l18.q: Find and correct the mistake: All cells have the exact same shape and size in every organism.

a.fix: Different types of cells usually have different shapes and sizes.

k6l18.raw: Different types of cells usually have different shapes and sizes.
k6l18.hint: Do nerve cells look the same as skin cells?
k6l18.expl: Cells vary in shape and size depending on their function, organism group, and organ.

k6l19.q: What are the three basic parts found in every cell?
opts: Cell membrane, cytoplasm, and nucleus (or nucleoid)

a.quiz: Cell membrane, cytoplasm, and nucleus (or nucleoid)

k6l19.hint: Think about structures common to prokaryotic, animal, and plant cells.
k6l19.expl: Every cell has a cell membrane, cytoplasm, and a nucleus (in eukaryotes) or nucleoid (in prokaryotes).

k6l19.q: Which part of the cell contains genetic material and acts as the control center?

a.quiz: Nucleus (or nucleoid)

k6l19.hint: This structure directs all life processes of the cell.
k6l19.expl: The nucleus or nucleoid houses genetic material and controls cell activities.

k6l19.q: How does a prokaryotic cell differ from a eukaryotic cell?
opts: Prokaryotic cells have chloroplasts, while eukaryotic cells do not
Prokaryotic cells lack a nuclear membrane and membrane-bound organelles
Prokaryotic cells are always larger than plant cells
Eukaryotic cells have no genetic material

a.quiz: Prokaryotic cells lack a nuclear membrane and membrane-bound organelles

k6l19.hint: Compare bacterial cells with plant and animal cells.
k6l19.expl: Prokaryotic cells (such as bacteria) lack a nuclear membrane and membrane-bound organelles, having only ribosomes in the cytoplasm.

k6l19.q: Which three structures are present in plant cells but absent in typical animal cells?
opts: Cell wall, chloroplasts, and a large central vacuole

a.quiz: Cell wall, chloroplasts, and a large central vacuole

k6l19.hint: Think about rigid support, green photosynthesis, and large storage sacs.
k6l19.expl: Plant cells possess a cell wall, chloroplasts (containing chlorophyll), and a large central vacuole.

k6l19.q: What is the main function of chloroplasts in plant leaf cells?
opts: To control water movement into roots
To absorb sunlight energy and synthesize organic matter during photosynthesis
To break down waste in bacteria

a.quiz: To absorb sunlight energy and synthesize organic matter during photosynthesis

k6l19.expl: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which captures solar energy to produce organic nutrients via photosynthesis.

k6l19.q: The ___ surrounds the cytoplasm and controls the exchange of substances with the environment.

a.quiz: cell membrane

k6l19.sentence: The cell membrane surrounds the cytoplasm.
k6l19.hint: It is the outer boundary present in every cell.
k6l19.expl: The cell membrane encloses the cell and regulates transport of materials in and out.

k6l19.q: Plant cells stay rigid without a skeleton because they are surrounded by a tough ___.

a.quiz: cell wall

k6l19.hint: It lies outside the plant cell membrane.
k6l19.expl: The cell wall protects the plant cell and maintains its fixed shape and rigidity.

k6l19.q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence.
k6l19.raw: The nucleus contains genetic material and controls all life activities of the cell.
k6l19.sentence: The nucleus contains genetic material and controls all life activities of the cell.
chunks: all life activities of the cell
k6l19.expl: This describes the main role of the nucleus.

k6l19.hint: Three structures are found in both animal and plant cells.
k6l19.expl: Chloroplasts are found in plant cells for photosynthesis, not in animal cells.

k6l19.q: Both animal cells and plant cells are eukaryotic cells with a true membrane-bound nucleus.
k6l19.hint: Compare prokaryotic bacteria with plants and animals.
k6l19.expl: Plants and animals are eukaryotes whose cells have a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles.

k6l19.q: Find and correct the mistake: Bacterial cells are eukaryotic cells because they have a nuclear membrane and chloroplasts.

a.fix: Bacterial cells are prokaryotic cells because they lack a nuclear membrane and membrane-bound organelles.

k6l19.raw: Bacterial cells are prokaryotic cells because they lack a nuclear membrane and membrane-bound organelles.
k6l19.expl: Bacteria are prokaryotes with a nucleoid (no nuclear membrane) and ribosomes as their only organelle.

k6l20.q: How do newly formed daughter cells grow into mature cells?
opts: Through metabolism, which increases their size and mass

a.quiz: Through metabolism, which increases their size and mass

k6l20.hint: Cells take in nutrients and convert energy.
k6l20.expl: Through metabolism, small daughter cells gradually increase in size and mass to become mature cells.

k6l20.q: What happens when a cell grows to a certain mature size?
opts: It divides into two daughter cells (cell reproduction)
It turns into a wooden table

a.quiz: It divides into two daughter cells (cell reproduction)

k6l20.hint: One parent cell produces two new cells.
k6l20.expl: When a cell reaches a certain size, it undergoes cell division (reproduction), splitting from one parent cell into two daughter cells.

k6l20.q: How does a multicellular organism like a corn plant or a human grow larger?
opts: By increasing both cell size and the number of cells
Only by absorbing rainwater without cell division
Only by keeping one single cell forever
By reducing the number of cells

a.quiz: By increasing both cell size and the number of cells

k6l20.hint: Think about both cell growth and cell division.
k6l20.expl: Multicellular organisms grow primarily through increases in both cell size and total cell number.

k6l20.q: Why do cells in an adult human body continue to divide even after height growth stops?
opts: To make the person 10 meters tall
To replace old, dead, and damaged cells such as cheek and stomach lining cells
To turn skin cells into plant leaves

a.quiz: To replace old, dead, and damaged cells such as cheek and stomach lining cells

k6l20.hint: Think about brushing your teeth or stomach acid.
k6l20.expl: Even after an organism stops growing in height, cell division continues to replace old, dead, and damaged cells.

k6l20.q: What can happen if cell division becomes uncontrolled in the body?
opts: Abnormal cell masses called tumors may form
All cells turn into red blood cells

a.quiz: Abnormal cell masses called tumors may form

k6l20.hint: Check the "Em có biết?" section on cell control.
k6l20.expl: When cell division escapes normal control and damaged cells divide continuously, tumors can form and disrupt normal body functions.

k6l20.q: Through ___, newly formed daughter cells increase in size and mass to become mature cells.

a.quiz: metabolism

k6l20.sentence: Daughter cells grow into mature cells through metabolism.
k6l20.hint: Think about nutrient absorption and energy conversion.
k6l20.expl: Metabolism allows young daughter cells to grow into mature cells.

k6l20.q: One parent cell divides into ___ daughter cells when it reaches a certain size.

a.quiz: two

k6l20.hint: Count the cells after one division in Figure 20.2.
k6l20.expl: Each dividing parent cell splits into two daughter cells (1 -> 2 -> 4).

k6l20.q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence.
k6l20.raw: Cell division replaces old, dead, and damaged cells in the body.
k6l20.sentence: Cell division replaces old, dead, and damaged cells in the body.
k6l20.expl: This highlights a key role of cell reproduction.

k6l20.hint: Three items are types of cells that no longer divide once fully differentiated.
k6l20.expl: Plant meristem cells at root tips and buds keep dividing, whereas differentiated nerve cells and mature red blood cells do not.

k6l20.q: Stomach lining cells are frequently damaged by stomach acid and are replaced every few days by cell division.
k6l20.expl: Corrosive stomach acid wears away surface stomach cells, so cell division replaces them every few days.

k6l20.q: Find and correct the mistake: A unicellular organism grows larger mainly by increasing its total number of cells.

a.fix: A unicellular organism grows larger by increasing the size of its single cell.

k6l20.raw: A unicellular organism grows larger by increasing the size of its single cell.
k6l20.hint: How many cells does a unicellular organism have?
k6l20.expl: A unicellular organism has only one cell, so its growth comes from an increase in that single cell’s size.

k6l21.q: Which tool is used to observe large fish egg cells in a petri dish?
opts: The naked eye or a magnifying glass (hand lens)

a.quiz: The naked eye or a magnifying glass (hand lens)

k6l21.hint: Fish eggs are much larger than microscopic plant cells.
k6l21.expl: Fish egg cells are large enough to be observed directly with the naked eye or a magnifying glass.

k6l21.q: Why should you lower the coverslip from one edge at an angle when preparing an onion cell slide?
opts: To crush the onion cells completely
To prevent air bubbles from getting trapped under the coverslip
To heat up the distilled water

a.quiz: To prevent air bubbles from getting trapped under the coverslip

k6l21.hint: Air bubbles can block your view under the microscope.
k6l21.expl: Sliding or lowering the coverslip from one edge pushes air out and prevents air bubbles from obscuring the specimen.

k6l21.q: What is used to absorb excess water around the coverslip after mounting the specimen?

a.quiz: Filter (blotting) paper

k6l21.expl: Filter/blotting paper is touched gently to the edge of the coverslip to absorb excess water.

k6l21.q: Which objective lenses are used in sequence to observe onion epidermal cells under the optical microscope?

a.quiz: First 10x, then switch to 40x

k6l21.hint: Start with lower magnification before higher magnification.
k6l21.expl: First locate the onion cells using the 10x objective lens, then switch to the 40x objective lens for detailed viewing.

k6l21.q: Which feature helps distinguish onion epidermal cells from fish egg cells?
opts: Onion cells are round and swim, while fish eggs are square
Onion cells are elongated/rectangular with a cell wall, while fish egg cells are spherical without a cell wall
Fish egg cells have green chloroplasts, while onion cells do not

a.quiz: Onion cells are elongated/rectangular with a cell wall, while fish egg cells are spherical without a cell wall

k6l21.hint: Compare plant cell shape and outer boundary with animal cell shape.
k6l21.expl: Onion epidermal cells are plant cells with a rigid cell wall and elongated rectangular shape, whereas fish egg cells are round animal cells lacking a cell wall.

k6l21.q: Place a drop of ___ onto the glass slide before laying down the thin onion epidermis.

a.quiz: distilled water

k6l21.sentence: Place a drop of distilled water onto the glass slide.
k6l21.hint: Use clean pure water to prepare the wet mount.
k6l21.expl: A drop of distilled water keeps the onion epidermis flat and hydrated on the glass slide.

k6l21.q: Use a ___ to gently stir and separate the fish eggs in the petri dish.

a.quiz: dissecting needle

k6l21.hint: A pointed lab tool used for handling delicate specimens.
k6l21.expl: A dissecting needle separates individual fish eggs gently without bursting them.

k6l21.q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence.
k6l21.raw: Slide the coverslip gently from one edge and blot excess water with filter paper.
k6l21.sentence: Slide the coverslip gently from one edge and blot excess water with filter paper.
k6l21.expl: This describes how to finish preparing a wet mount slide.

k6l21.hint: Three items are used to prepare the onion epidermal wet mount.
k6l21.expl: A separatory funnel is used to separate immiscible liquids, not to prepare microscope slides.

k6l21.q: Both onion epidermal cells and fish egg cells contain cytoplasm and a nucleus.
k6l21.hint: Think about the basic parts shared by plant and animal cells.
k6l21.expl: Both plant (onion) and animal (fish egg) cells are eukaryotic cells with cell membrane, cytoplasm, and nucleus.

k6l21.q: Find and correct the mistake: Observe fish egg cells only at 100x magnification and onion epidermal cells with the naked eye.

a.fix: Observe fish egg cells with the naked eye or hand lens, and onion epidermal cells with an optical microscope.

k6l21.raw: Observe fish egg cells with the naked eye or hand lens, and onion epidermal cells with an optical microscope.
k6l21.hint: Which cell is large enough to see without a microscope?
k6l21.expl: Fish egg cells are large and visible to the naked eye/hand lens, while microscopic onion cells require an optical microscope.

opts: Any object that uses gasoline and releases exhaust gas
An individual living entity capable of performing basic life processes
Any object made of metal or stone
A non-living cage at the zoo

a.quiz: An individual living entity capable of performing basic life processes

k6l22.hint: Think about nutrition, respiration, sensitivity, growth, excretion, and reproduction.
k6l22.expl: An organism is a living individual capable of carrying out basic life processes such as nutrition, respiration, growth, sensitivity, excretion, and reproduction.

k6l22.q: Why is a car NOT a living organism even though it takes in oxygen and releases carbon dioxide?
opts: Because cars are too large to have cells
Because a car is not made of cells and cannot grow, reproduce, or perform life processes
Because cars do not move on roads

a.quiz: Because a car is not made of cells and cannot grow, reproduce, or perform life processes

k6l22.hint: Compare fuel combustion in an engine with all characteristics of life.
k6l22.expl: Unlike living things, a car is not composed of cells and cannot grow, metabolize nutrients, or reproduce.

k6l22.q: Which group lists ONLY unicellular organisms?

a.quiz: Bacterium, baker’s yeast, and amoeba

k6l22.hint: Unicellular means made of just one cell.
k6l22.expl: Bacteria, baker’s yeast, and amoebae are single-celled (unicellular) organisms.

k6l22.q: How are life processes carried out in a multicellular organism?
opts: Only one single cell does everything while all other cells rest
Different types of specialized cells perform distinct functions and coordinate together
Each cell lives completely independently outside the body

a.quiz: Different types of specialized cells perform distinct functions and coordinate together

k6l22.hint: Think about specialization and coordination among many cells.
k6l22.expl: In multicellular organisms, different cell types specialize in particular functions and work together to sustain the whole organism.

k6l22.q: Why can we see a frog with the naked eye, whereas we need a microscope to see an amoeba?
opts: Because an amoeba is made of glass
Because a frog is a multicellular organism with millions of cells, while an amoeba is a single tiny cell

a.quiz: Because a frog is a multicellular organism with millions of cells, while an amoeba is a single tiny cell

k6l22.hint: Compare the number of cells in each organism.
k6l22.expl: Organism size largely depends on cell number: a frog is multicellular, whereas an amoeba consists of a single microscopic cell.

k6l22.q: A ___ organism consists of only one cell that performs all basic life processes.

a.quiz: unicellular

k6l22.sentence: A unicellular organism consists of only one cell.
k6l22.expl: Unicellular organisms such as bacteria and yeast are made of a single cell.

k6l22.q: Taking in oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide through breathing is the life process of ___.

a.quiz: respiration

k6l22.hint: Think about inhaling oxygen and exhaling carbon dioxide.
k6l22.expl: Respiration is the process of taking in oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide.

k6l22.q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence.
k6l22.raw: A multicellular organism is made of many cells that work together.
k6l22.sentence: A multicellular organism is made of many cells that work together.
k6l22.expl: This describes how multicellular organisms are organized.
An amoeba is a unicellular organism, whereas a rabbit, frog, and kumquat tree are multicellular.

k6l22.q: Green algae (tảo lục) and tetanus bacteria (vi khuẩn uốn ván) are examples of unicellular organisms.
k6l22.expl: Both unicellular green algae and bacteria consist of single cells and are classified as unicellular organisms.

k6l22.q: Find and correct the mistake: Baker’s yeast and bacteria are multicellular organisms made of millions of cells.

a.fix: Baker’s yeast and bacteria are unicellular organisms made of a single cell.

k6l22.raw: Baker’s yeast and bacteria are unicellular organisms made of a single cell.
k6l22.hint: How many cells make up a bacterium or baker’s yeast?
k6l22.expl: Bacteria and baker’s yeast are microscopic unicellular organisms consisting of just one cell.

k6l23.q: What is the correct order of organization in a multicellular organism from lowest to highest?
opts: Organ -> Tissue -> Cell -> Organism -> Organ system
Cell -> Tissue -> Organ -> Organ system -> Organism
Tissue -> Cell -> Organ system -> Organ -> Organism
Organism -> Organ system -> Organ -> Tissue -> Cell

a.quiz: Cell -> Tissue -> Organ -> Organ system -> Organism

k6l23.hint: Start with the smallest basic unit of life.
k6l23.expl: Multicellular organisms are organized hierarchically from cell -> tissue -> organ -> organ system -> organism.

k6l23.q: What is a tissue in a multicellular organism?
opts: A single organ like the heart
A group of similar cells connected together to perform a specific function

a.quiz: A group of similar cells connected together to perform a specific function

k6l23.hint: Cells combine to form this next level.
k6l23.expl: A tissue consists of many cells sharing the same function linked together, such as muscle tissue or leaf epidermal tissue.

k6l23.q: Which plant tissue transports water and minerals upward from the roots to the leaves?

a.quiz: Xylem tissue (mô mạch gỗ)

k6l23.hint: Think of the woody vascular tissue in plants.
k6l23.expl: Xylem (mô mạch gỗ) conducts water and mineral salts from roots to leaves, while phloem transports organic nutrients.

k6l23.q: Which organs make up the human respiratory system?

a.quiz: Nose, trachea, and lungs

k6l23.hint: Think about the organs involved in breathing and gas exchange.
k6l23.expl: The nose, trachea, and lungs cooperate in the respiratory system to take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide.

k6l23.q: What are the two main organ systems in a flowering plant?

a.quiz: Root system and shoot system

k6l23.hint: One system grows underground and the other grows above ground.
k6l23.expl: Flowering plants are organized into two main organ systems: the root system (hệ rễ) and the shoot system (hệ chồi).

k6l23.q: A group of similar cells working together to perform a specific function is called a ___.

a.quiz: tissue

k6l23.sentence: A group of similar cells forms a tissue.
k6l23.hint: It is the level right above the cell.
k6l23.expl: Cells performing the same function connect together to form a tissue.

k6l23.q: In flowering plants, the ___ absorbs water and minerals from the soil.

a.quiz: root

k6l23.expl: Roots anchor the plant and absorb water and dissolved minerals from the soil.

k6l23.q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence.
k6l23.raw: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form organ systems, and organ systems form an organism.
k6l23.sentence: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form organ systems, and organ systems form an organism.
chunks: and organ systems form an organism
k6l23.expl: This shows the five levels of organization in multicellular bodies.
Phloem tissue is a plant tissue, whereas the heart, stomach, and lungs are human organs.

k6l23.q: If one organ in the body is diseased or injured, the entire organism is affected because organ systems work closely together.
k6l23.hint: Think about how organs and organ systems depend on one another.
k6l23.expl: Because organs and organ systems coordinate to sustain life processes, damage to one organ affects the whole body.

k6l23.q: Find and correct the mistake: Phloem tissue transports water and minerals from roots to leaves, while xylem transports organic food from leaves.

a.fix: Xylem tissue transports water and minerals from roots to leaves, while phloem transports organic nutrients from leaves.

k6l23.raw: Xylem tissue transports water and minerals from roots to leaves, while phloem transports organic nutrients from leaves.
k6l23.hint: Swap xylem and phloem to match their transport roles.
k6l23.expl: Xylem conducts water and minerals upward from roots; phloem conducts organic substances made in leaves to other plant parts.

k6l6.q: What is the standard base unit of mass in Vietnam and the SI system?

a.quiz: Kilogram (kg)

k6l6.expl: In Vietnam’s legal measurement system and the SI system, the base unit of mass is the kilogram (kg).

k6l6.q: What is the second step when using a dial scale to measure mass?
opts: Adjust the zero screw so the pointer is exactly at the zero mark

a.quiz: Adjust the zero screw so the pointer is exactly at the zero mark

k6l6.hint: Make sure the pointer starts at 0.
k6l6.expl: Before placing the object on the pan, adjust the zero screw so the pointer aligns with the 0 mark.

k6l6.q: What does the "Tare" button on an electronic balance do?
opts: Subtracts the mass of the container automatically
Changes the unit from grams to meters

a.quiz: Subtracts the mass of the container automatically

k6l6.hint: Used when weighing powder or liquid inside a cup/beaker.
k6l6.expl: Pressing Tare with the empty container on the pan zeroes the display so only the sample’s mass is measured.

k6l6.q: Which action is a mistake when using a dial scale or electronic balance?
opts: Placing the scale on a flat, level surface
Looking perpendicular to the dial face
Placing an object off-center or on an uneven surface
Reading the result after the balance becomes steady

a.quiz: Placing an object off-center or on an uneven surface

k6l6.hint: The balance needs a level surface and centered load.
k6l6.expl: Placing a scale on an uneven surface or putting the object off-center causes inaccurate readings and can damage the balance.

k6l6.q: How many kilograms are in 1 metric ton (1 tấn)?
k6l6.expl: One metric ton (1 tấn) equals 1,000 kilograms (and 1 tạ equals 100 kg).

k6l6.q: ___ is the measure of the amount of matter in an object.

a.quiz: Mass

k6l6.sentence: Mass is the measure of the amount of matter.
k6l6.hint: Think about how much matter a full cup of milk has compared to water.
k6l6.expl: Mass measures the amount of matter in an object; its base unit is the kilogram (kg).

k6l6.q: On an electronic balance, press ___ to subtract the mass of a beaker or cup.

a.quiz: Tare

k6l6.hint: It deducts the container weight automatically.
k6l6.expl: Pressing Tare zeroes the balance with the container placed on it.

k6l6.q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence.
k6l6.raw: The kilogram (kg) is the standard base unit of mass in Vietnam.
k6l6.sentence: The kilogram (kg) is the standard base unit of mass in Vietnam.
k6l6.expl: This states the base unit of mass.

k6l6.hint: Three items are mass balances or scales.
k6l6.expl: A stopwatch measures time, not mass.

k6l6.q: Always place the balance on a flat surface and read the result when the scale is steady.
k6l6.expl: A level surface, centered load, and waiting for a steady reading ensure accuracy.

k6l6.q: Find and correct the mistake: Put a much heavier object than the scale’s measuring range onto a dial scale.

a.fix: Estimate the mass first and choose a scale with a suitable measuring range.

k6l6.raw: Estimate the mass first and choose a scale with a suitable measuring range.
k6l6.hint: What happens if an object is too heavy for the scale?
k6l6.expl: Overloading a scale beyond its measuring range can damage the spring or mechanism and give wrong results.

k6l24.q: Which unicellular organism from pond water can perform photosynthesis and is recognized by its green color?

a.quiz: Euglena (trùng roi xanh)

k6l24.hint: Look for the green photosynthetic organism in Figure 24.2.
k6l24.expl: Euglena (trùng roi xanh) is green due to chlorophyll and can perform photosynthesis.

k6l24.q: Which organs belong to the human digestive system?
opts: Mouth, esophagus, stomach, intestines, liver, and pancreas

a.quiz: Mouth, esophagus, stomach, intestines, liver, and pancreas

k6l24.hint: Think about digesting and absorbing food.
k6l24.expl: The digestive system consists of the mouth, esophagus, stomach, intestines, liver, pancreas, and anus.

k6l24.q: What is the main function of the human circulatory system?
opts: Transmitting nerve signals between body parts
Transporting oxygen and nutrients and removing carbon dioxide and wastes
Breaking down food in the stomach

a.quiz: Transporting oxygen and nutrients and removing carbon dioxide and wastes

k6l24.hint: Think about the heart, blood vessels, and blood.
k6l24.expl: The circulatory system transports oxygen and nutrients to body cells and carries carbon dioxide and waste products away.

k6l24.q: Which organs make up the human nervous system?
opts: Brain, spinal cord, ganglia, and nerves

a.quiz: Brain, spinal cord, ganglia, and nerves

k6l24.hint: This system transmits information and signals across the body.
k6l24.expl: The nervous system comprises the brain, spinal cord, ganglia, and nerves to transmit signals and coordinate activities.

k6l24.q: When preparing a pond water slide, what is used to absorb water overflowing outside the coverslip?

a.quiz: Filter paper

k6l24.hint: Use absorbent paper around the edge of the coverslip.
k6l24.expl: Filter paper is used to blot away excess water overflowing outside the coverslip before viewing under the microscope.

k6l24.q: The ___ system includes the heart, blood vessels, and blood to transport oxygen and nutrients.

a.quiz: circulatory

k6l24.sentence: The circulatory system transports oxygen and nutrients.
k6l24.hint: It pumps blood throughout the body.
k6l24.expl: The circulatory system transports oxygen and nutrients and carries away wastes.

k6l24.q: The ___ system consists of the brain, spinal cord, ganglia, and nerves.

a.quiz: nervous

k6l24.hint: It transmits signals across the body.
k6l24.expl: The nervous system transmits information and signals between parts of the body.

k6l24.q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence.
k6l24.raw: The digestive system breaks down food, absorbs nutrients, and eliminates waste.
k6l24.sentence: The digestive system breaks down food, absorbs nutrients, and eliminates waste.
k6l24.expl: This states the function of the digestive system.

k6l24.hint: Three items are unicellular organisms in pond water.
k6l24.expl: The stomach is a human digestive organ, whereas paramecium, euglena, and rod bacteria are unicellular organisms.

k6l24.q: Pond water slides are observed under the optical microscope using 10x and 40x objective lenses.
k6l24.hint: Check the lab procedure in section II.1.
k6l24.expl: Unicellular organisms in pond water are microscopic and observed at 10x and 40x.

k6l24.q: Find and correct the mistake: The nervous system pumps blood through blood vessels to deliver nutrients.

a.fix: The circulatory system pumps blood through blood vessels to deliver nutrients.

k6l24.raw: The circulatory system pumps blood through blood vessels to deliver nutrients.
k6l24.hint: Which system uses the heart and blood vessels?
k6l24.expl: The circulatory system transports blood, while the nervous system transmits signals via the brain, spinal cord, and nerves.

k6l25.q: What is the correct order of taxonomic ranks from largest to smallest?
opts: Species -> Genus -> Family -> Order -> Class -> Phylum -> Kingdom
Kingdom -> Phylum -> Class -> Order -> Family -> Genus -> Species
Kingdom -> Class -> Phylum -> Family -> Order -> Species -> Genus
Phylum -> Kingdom -> Order -> Class -> Genus -> Family -> Species

a.quiz: Kingdom -> Phylum -> Class -> Order -> Family -> Genus -> Species

k6l25.hint: Start with Kingdom (giới) and end with Species (loài).
k6l25.expl: From largest to smallest, the seven taxonomic ranks are: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, and Species.

k6l25.q: Which kingdom includes unicellular prokaryotic organisms such as bacteria?

a.quiz: Kingdom Monera (Giới Khởi sinh)

k6l25.hint: Monera consists of unicellular prokaryotes without a nuclear membrane.
k6l25.expl: Kingdom Monera comprises unicellular prokaryotic organisms such as bacteria.

k6l25.q: To which kingdom do amoebae and euglenas belong?

a.quiz: Kingdom Protista (Giới Nguyên sinh)

k6l25.hint: They are mostly unicellular eukaryotic organisms.
k6l25.expl: Amoeba and euglena are mostly single-celled eukaryotes belonging to Kingdom Protista.

k6l25.q: How is a species scientific name written according to binomial nomenclature?
opts: In all capital letters with three words
In italics with two parts: capitalized Genus followed by lowercase species (e.g., Apis cerana)

a.quiz: In italics with two parts: capitalized Genus followed by lowercase species (e.g., Apis cerana)

k6l25.hint: Look at the example Apis cerana (Asian honeybee).
k6l25.expl: Scientific names are two-part Latin names written in italics: the capitalized genus name followed by the lowercase species name.

k6l25.q: In Figure 25.5, which kingdom do a mango tree and green moss belong to?

a.quiz: Kingdom Plantae (Giới Thực vật)

k6l25.expl: Mango trees and mosses are multicellular, eukaryotic autotrophs belonging to Kingdom Plantae.

k6l25.q: In the taxonomic hierarchy, ___ is the largest rank and species is the smallest rank.

a.quiz: kingdom

k6l25.sentence: Kingdom is the largest taxonomic rank.
k6l25.expl: Kingdom is the broadest taxonomic rank, encompassing multiple phyla.

k6l25.q: Mushrooms and yeasts belong to Kingdom ___.

a.quiz: Fungi

k6l25.hint: This kingdom includes unicellular yeasts and multicellular mushrooms.
k6l25.expl: Kingdom Fungi consists of eukaryotic organisms such as mushrooms, molds, and yeasts.

k6l25.q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence.
k6l25.raw: Living organisms are divided into five kingdoms: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.
k6l25.sentence: Living organisms are divided into five kingdoms: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.
k6l25.expl: This names all five kingdoms proposed by R.H. Whittaker.

k6l25.hint: Three organisms belong to Kingdom Animalia.
k6l25.expl: A lotus plant belongs to Kingdom Plantae, whereas a lion, honeybee, and gecko belong to Kingdom Animalia.

k6l25.q: Biological classification helps us find species easily and shows similarities and relationships among organism groups.
k6l25.hint: Think about why books in a bookstore and organisms in nature are grouped.
k6l25.expl: Classification organizes organisms by shared traits so we can identify them and understand their relationships.

k6l25.q: Find and correct the mistake: Bacteria belong to Kingdom Protista because they are multicellular eukaryotes.

a.fix: Bacteria belong to Kingdom Monera because they are unicellular prokaryotes.

k6l25.raw: Bacteria belong to Kingdom Monera because they are unicellular prokaryotes.
k6l25.expl: Bacteria are unicellular prokaryotic organisms placed in Kingdom Monera, whereas Protista consists mostly of unicellular eukaryotes.

k6l26.q: What is the core principle of a dichotomous key?
opts: Grouping all organisms into one single box
Splitting a group of organisms into two subgroups with contrasting traits at each step
Arranging organisms alphabetically by Vietnamese name only
Counting the age of trees in a forest

a.quiz: Splitting a group of organisms into two subgroups with contrasting traits at each step

k6l26.expl: A dichotomous key repeatedly divides organisms into two groups based on opposite (contrasting) characteristics until each species is identified.

k6l26.q: In Figure 26.2, which trait separates the climbing perch (cá rô) from the eel (con lươn)?
opts: Presence or absence of scales (scales vs. no scales)

a.quiz: Presence or absence of scales (scales vs. no scales)

k6l26.hint: Both fish lack legs, so look at their skin covering.
k6l26.expl: Both climbing perch and eels have no legs; climbing perch has scales, whereas the eel has no scales.

k6l26.q: According to the dichotomous key in Figure 26.2, how are the dragonfly and greenbottle fly separated?
opts: Dragonfly has 4 wings; greenbottle fly has 2 wings
Dragonfly has 8 legs; greenbottle fly has 10 legs
Dragonfly has scales; greenbottle fly has fur
Dragonfly lives underground; greenbottle fly lives in the ocean

a.quiz: Dragonfly has 4 wings; greenbottle fly has 2 wings

k6l26.hint: Count the number of wings on each insect.
k6l26.expl: Both have legs and wings; the dragonfly has 4 wings while the greenbottle fly has 2 wings.

k6l26.q: Which animal in Figure 26.2 has legs, no wings, and 8 legs?

a.quiz: House spider (nhện nhà)

k6l26.expl: In Figure 26.2, the house spider (nhện nhà) is wingless and has 8 legs, while the field crab has 10 legs.

k6l26.q: When do you stop splitting groups while building a dichotomous key?
opts: After only one split regardless of species count
When every individual species has been separated and identified
Whenever two species still share the exact same branch

a.quiz: When every individual species has been separated and identified

k6l26.hint: Each end branch of the diagram should lead to one species.
k6l26.expl: You continue dividing smaller subgroups by contrasting traits until each individual species is uniquely identified.

k6l26.q: A ___ divides a group of organisms into two subgroups with contrasting traits at each step.

a.quiz: dichotomous key

k6l26.sentence: A dichotomous key divides organisms into two groups.
k6l26.hint: It is the most common biological classification key.
k6l26.expl: A dichotomous key splits organisms into pairs of contrasting traits until each species is identified.

k6l26.q: In Figure 26.2, a field crab has ___ legs and no wings.
k6l26.hint: Compare the leg count of a house spider (8) and a field crab.
k6l26.expl: A field crab has 10 legs and no wings, distinguishing it from the 8-legged house spider.

k6l26.q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence.
k6l26.raw: A dichotomous key divides an initial group of organisms into two groups with contrasting traits.
k6l26.sentence: A dichotomous key divides an initial group of organisms into two groups with contrasting traits.
chunks: into two groups with contrasting traits
k6l26.expl: This defines how a dichotomous key works.

k6l26.hint: Three animals have legs in Figure 26.2.
k6l26.expl: An eel has no legs, whereas a dragonfly, house spider, and field crab all have legs.

k6l26.q: Both the dragonfly and the greenbottle fly have legs and wings, but the dragonfly has 4 wings while the greenbottle fly has 2 wings.
k6l26.hint: Check the winged branch in Figure 26.2.
k6l26.expl: The dragonfly has 4 wings and the greenbottle fly has 2 wings.

k6l26.q: Find and correct the mistake: A house spider has 10 legs and 2 wings, while a field crab has 8 legs.

a.fix: A house spider has 8 legs and no wings, while a field crab has 10 legs and no wings.

k6l26.raw: A house spider has 8 legs and no wings, while a field crab has 10 legs and no wings.
k6l26.hint: Check the wingless branch in Figure 26.2.
k6l26.expl: Neither spiders nor crabs have wings; a house spider has 8 legs and a field crab has 10 legs.

k6l27.q: What are the three typical shapes of bacteria?

a.quiz: Rod (bacillus), spiral (spirillum), and spherical (coccus)

k6l27.hint: Think of trực khuẩn, xoắn khuẩn, and cầu khuẩn.
k6l27.expl: Bacteria exhibit three classic shapes: rod-shaped (bacilli), spiral-shaped (spirilla), and spherical (cocci).

k6l27.q: What is the function of the flagellum (roi) in many bacteria?
opts: To digest food in the stomach

a.quiz: To help the bacterium move

k6l27.hint: It acts like a microscopic propeller or tail.
k6l27.expl: Many bacteria possess a whip-like flagellum for locomotion and short pili for attaching to host cells.

k6l27.q: How do decomposer bacteria benefit nature?
opts: They break down dead organisms and animal wastes into nutrients for plants

a.quiz: They break down dead organisms and animal wastes into nutrients for plants

k6l27.hint: Check Figure 27.3 on the role of bacteria in nature.
k6l27.expl: Decomposer bacteria break down dead organisms and animal waste into nutrients that enrich the soil for plants.

k6l27.q: How is cholera (bệnh tả) transmitted, and what are its main symptoms?
opts: Through mosquito bites; causes green skin
Through contaminated food and water; causes diarrhea, vomiting, and high fever
Through loud noise; causes ear pain

a.quiz: Through contaminated food and water; causes diarrhea, vomiting, and high fever

k6l27.hint: Check the description of cholera in section IV.
k6l27.expl: Cholera is caused by cholera bacteria transmitted via contaminated food and drink, leading to diarrhea, vomiting, and high fever.

k6l27.q: Why should antibiotics NOT be used carelessly without a doctor’s prescription?
opts: Because improper use causes antibiotic resistance, making infections harder to treat
Because antibiotics are made of spoiled food
Because antibiotics cure all viral colds instantly

a.quiz: Because improper use causes antibiotic resistance, making infections harder to treat

k6l27.hint: Bacteria can adapt when exposed improperly to antibiotics.
k6l27.expl: Misusing antibiotics without medical guidance leads to antibiotic resistance, reducing treatment effectiveness.

k6l27.q: Many bacteria have a whip-like ___ for movement and short pili for attaching to host cells.

a.quiz: flagellum

k6l27.sentence: Many bacteria have a flagellum for movement.
k6l27.hint: Think of the tail-like structure in Figure 27.2.
k6l27.expl: The flagellum enables bacterial movement, while pili help bacteria attach to host cells.

k6l27.q: Lactic acid bacteria carry out ___ to produce yogurt, pickled vegetables, and cheese.

a.quiz: fermentation

k6l27.hint: They convert sugars into lactic acid without oxygen.
k6l27.expl: Fermentation by lactic acid bacteria creates the characteristic aroma and sour taste of yogurt and pickles.

k6l27.q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence.
k6l27.raw: Bacteria are unicellular prokaryotic organisms with rod, spiral, or spherical shapes.
k6l27.sentence: Bacteria are unicellular prokaryotic organisms with rod, spiral, or spherical shapes.
k6l27.expl: This summarizes bacterial cell type and main shapes.

k6l27.hint: Three items are diseases caused by bacteria.
k6l27.expl: Photosynthesis is a plant process, whereas tuberculosis, cholera, and tetanus are bacterial diseases.

k6l27.q: Most bacteria are beneficial to humans and nature, helping digestion, food production, and waste decomposition.
k6l27.hint: Are most bacteria helpful or harmful?
k6l27.expl: The majority of bacteria are beneficial—supporting human immunity/digestion, nutrient cycling, and food fermentation.

k6l27.q: Find and correct the mistake: Bacterial cells have a membrane-bound nucleus and chloroplasts like green plant cells.

k6l27.raw: Bacterial cells are prokaryotic with a nucleoid (no nuclear membrane) and have no chloroplasts.

k6l28.q: Why should you use plain (unsweetened) yogurt rather than sweetened yogurt when observing bacteria?
opts: Sugar and additives in sweetened yogurt interfere with preparing and viewing the bacterial slide

a.quiz: Sugar and additives in sweetened yogurt interfere with preparing and viewing the bacterial slide

k6l28.hint: Check the warning in the textbook preparation section.
k6l28.expl: Plain (unsweetened) yogurt is used because added sugar and flavorings in sweetened yogurt obscure the microscopic view of bacteria.

k6l28.q: Why must boiled water be cooled to about 50°C before adding the starter yogurt?
opts: Boiling water makes the glass jars turn blue
Boiling water would kill the beneficial lactic acid bacteria in the starter yogurt
Cold water melts the foam box

k6l28.q: How long should the yogurt mixture be incubated in a covered foam box?

a.quiz: 10 to 12 hours

k6l28.hint: Check Step 3 of the yogurt-making procedure.
k6l28.expl: Keeping the jars warm in a covered foam box for 10 to 12 hours provides ideal conditions for lactic acid fermentation.

k6l28.q: What happens if fermented yogurt is left at warm room temperature instead of being refrigerated after incubation?
opts: It turns back into dry milk powder
Bacteria continue fermenting rapidly, making the yogurt overly sour and spoiled

a.quiz: Bacteria continue fermenting rapidly, making the yogurt overly sour and spoiled

k6l28.q: In Gram staining, what colors do Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria appear under the microscope?
opts: Gram-positive is purple; Gram-negative is pink-red
Gram-positive is green; Gram-negative is yellow
Gram-positive is blue; Gram-negative is white

a.quiz: Gram-positive is purple; Gram-negative is pink-red

k6l28.hint: Check the "Em có biết?" section on Hans Christian Joachim Gram.
k6l28.expl: After Gram staining, Gram-positive bacteria stain purple, whereas Gram-negative bacteria (which include most disease-causing bacteria) stain pink-red.

k6l28.q: Dilute one spoon of ___ yogurt with 10 mL of distilled water before placing a drop on the glass slide.

a.quiz: plain

k6l28.sentence: Dilute one spoon of plain yogurt with distilled water.

Solar energy, nuclear energy, and tidal energy
Only light energy and zero heat

k6l48.q: Why do you feel warmth when rubbing your two hands together on a cold day?
opts: Mechanical/motion energy from rubbing transforms into thermal energy (heat)
Because hands produce electricity from air

k6l48.q: In Question 4a on page 169, chemical energy stored in food we eat transforms into what to help us ride a bicycle?

k6l48.q: Energy is neither created nor destroyed; it only transforms or ___ from one object to another.

k6l48.hint: Truyền từ vật này sang vật khác.
k6l48.expl: The law of conservation of energy states energy transforms or transfers while total energy is conserved.

k6l48.q: When a ball rises into the air, its ___ energy converts into potential energy.

a.quiz: kinetic

k6l48.hint: Động năng chuyển hóa thành thế năng khi đi lên.
k6l48.expl: Upward motion converts kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy.

k6l48.q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence.

k6l48.expl: This describes energy transformation during a ball’s flight.

k6l48.hint: Three items are energy forms in the word box on page 170.
k6l48.expl: A wooden bench is furniture, whereas kinetic energy, potential energy, and thermal energy are forms of energy.

k6l48.q: Total energy is always conserved and never disappears or is created from nothing.
k6l48.hint: Check blank (9)–(10) and "Em đã học" on page 170.
k6l48.expl: Total energy remains conserved throughout energy transformations and transfers.

k6l48.q: Find and correct the mistake: A dropped ball bounces higher than its release height because energy is created out of nowhere during the bounce.

k6l49.q: Does wasted energy (năng lượng hao phí) ever appear when energy transforms from one form to another?
opts: Yes, wasted energy always appears during energy transformation and transfer
No, wasted energy never exists in any machine or lamp
Only when no energy is used

k6l49.hint: Check the lesson objective and "Em đã học" on pages 171–172.
k6l49.expl: Wasted energy always occurs during energy conversion and transfer, commonly as thermal energy (and sometimes sound or light).

Incandescent: 95 J light, 5 J heat; LED: 5 J light, 95 J heat
Both produce 100 J light and 0 J heat
Both produce 0 J light and 100 J heat

k6l49.hint: Compare the three boiling methods on page 171.

k6l49.q: Which form does wasted energy most commonly take during energy use?

LED lamps waste 99% of electricity as heat
LED lamps require burning coal inside the room
Incandescent bulbs last longer and use less power

k6l49.hint: Check Figure 49.3 and the "Em có thể" box on page 172.
k6l49.expl: LED lighting uses electrical energy far more efficiently for visible light and wastes much less energy as heat than incandescent bulbs.

k6l49.q: Wasted energy always appears during energy conversion and often appears as ___ energy.

k6l49.expl: Wasted energy commonly takes the form of thermal energy.

k6l49.q: In Figure 49.3, a 100 J ___ lamp produces 80 J of visible light and 20 J of heat.

k6l49.expl: LED lamps deliver 80 J of visible light out of 100 J electrical input.

k6l49.q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence.

chunks: and the rest is wasted energy
k6l49.expl: This states the split between useful and wasted energy.

k6l49.q: When a car runs on the road, wasted energy can appear as thermal energy and sound energy.

k6l50.q: Which of the following are renewable energy sources (Question 1b on page 174: coal, gasoline, Sun, natural gas, wind)?

k6l50.q: How do non-renewable energy sources differ from renewable energy sources?
opts: Non-renewable sources take millions to hundreds of millions of years to form and will deplete, whereas renewable sources are naturally available and replenished quickly
Non-renewable sources grow back every hour; renewable sources disappear forever after one use
There is no difference between them

k6l50.hint: Check section I and Question 1a on pages 173–174.
k6l50.expl: Non-renewable sources form over millions of years and cannot be quickly replaced, while renewable sources are continuously replenished in nature.

k6l50.q: According to Figure 50.2a and 50.3b, what can solar panels and solar water heaters do?
opts: Solar panels convert sunlight into electrical energy; solar water heaters can heat water above 60°C
Solar panels turn water into solid iron
Solar water heaters freeze water to -50°C
Solar energy only works inside dark caves

k6l50.q: Which five renewable energy icons are shown on the left of Figure 50.1a?
opts: Sun (Mặt Trời), Wind (Gió), Water (Nước), Geothermal (Địa nhiệt), and Biomass (Sinh khối)
Coal, crude oil, natural gas, uranium, and plastic
Gold, silver, copper, lead, and tin

k6l50.hint: Look at the left column of Figure 50.1 on page 173.
k6l50.expl: Figure 50.1a shows renewable sources: Sun, Wind, Water, Geothermal, and Biomass.

k6l50.q: What warning is given in the "Em có biết?" box on page 175 about rapid growth in solar electricity?
opts: Large amounts of used solar panels within ~20 years could create waste containing toxic chemicals if not managed properly
Sunlight will turn into black ice next year
Solar panels produce infinite free food inside
Wind will stop blowing on Earth

k6l50.hint: Check the "Em có biết?" box on page 175.
k6l50.expl: Scientists warn that spent solar panels can become hazardous chemical waste in ~20 years without proper recycling/management.

k6l50.q: ___ energy is naturally available and continuously replenished by natural processes, such as solar or wind power.

k6l50.sentence: Solar and wind are renewable energy sources.
k6l50.expl: Renewable energy sources replenish naturally and are less harmful to the environment than fossil fuels.

k6l50.q: Heat energy obtained from inside the Earth or hot springs is called ___ energy.

k6l50.expl: Geothermal energy harnesses heat from inside the Earth.

k6l50.sentence: Renewable energy sources include solar, wind, water, biomass, and geothermal energy.
k6l50.expl: This names five renewable energy sources.

k6l50.hint: Three items are renewable energy sources in Figure 50.1a.

k6l50.raw: Crude oil, coal, and natural gas are non-renewable fossil fuels that take millions of years to form.
k6l50.expl: Coal, oil, and natural gas formed over millions of years and are non-renewable.

k6l51.q: What are the three main benefits of saving energy listed in section I and "Em đã học"?
opts: Saves costs, conserves non-renewable energy sources, and helps reduce waste and environmental pollution
Increases air pollution and wastes more money

a) Sun-drying wet clothes instead of using a dryer

d) Unplugging or turning off devices when not in use

k6l51.hint: Look for the wasteful habit in list a–i.
k6l51.expl: Leaving a TV on all day wastes electrical energy unnecessarily.

k6l51.q: Why should we limit single-use plastic bags, plastic bottles, and plastic straws and use paper bags, reusable bottles, and paper straws instead (Question 1b on page 178)?

Because plastic bags dissolve into drinking water in 1 second
Because paper is heavier than steel

k6l51.expl: Replacing single-use plastics/nylon with reusable or paper alternatives reduces long-lasting plastic waste and environmental harm.

k6l51.expl: Taking advantage of natural daylight reduces unnecessary daytime lighting power.

k6l51.q: ___ or recycling paper, plastic, and cardboard boxes reduces waste and conserves resources.

k6l51.expl: Reusing and recycling items cuts waste and saves materials and energy.

k6l51.sentence: Energy saving saves money, conserves non-renewable energy, and reduces waste and pollution.

Leaving the TV on all day wastes energy, whereas LED lighting, unplugging idle appliances, and turning off taps while brushing teeth save resources.

k6l51.q: Find and correct the mistake: Burning more non-renewable fossil fuels recklessly has zero impact on costs, fuel reserves, or air pollution.

k6l52.q: Why do we see the Sun rise in the east and set in the west each day?
opts: Because Earth rotates around its axis from west to east, making the Sun’s east-to-west motion an apparent motion
Because the Sun physically flies around Earth every 24 hours while Earth stays motionless
Because the Sun turns off at noon

a.quiz: Because Earth rotates around its axis from west to east, making the Sun’s east-to-west motion an apparent motion

k6l52.expl: Earth’s real rotation from west to east makes the Sun appear to move across the sky from east to west.

k6l52.q: How long does it take Earth to rotate once around its axis?

a.quiz: 24 hours (one day–night cycle)

k6l52.expl: Earth completes one rotation around its axis in 24 hours.

k6l52.q: How do a star, a planet, and a natural satellite differ in light emission and motion?

Satellites orbit stars and stars orbit moons

k6l52.hint: Check section III and "Em đã học" on page 181.
k6l52.expl: Stars are self-luminous; planets orbit stars without emitting their own light; natural satellites orbit planets without emitting their own light.

k6l52.q: In Figure 52.3, satellite photos of Earth show only about half of Earth at a time, and Earth rotates once in 24 hours. At least how many hours apart could two photos showing opposite/half views be taken (or half a rotation)?

k6l52.hint: Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours, so half a turn (180°) takes 12 hours.
k6l52.expl: Because Earth is spherical and rotates once every 24 hours, half a rotation takes 12 hours (and a full cycle back to the same orientation takes 24 hours).

k6l52.hint: Check the question on page 181 and the definition of thiên thể.
k6l52.expl: Sputnik is an artificial satellite built by humans, not a natural celestial body.

k6l52.q: Because Earth rotates from west to ___, the Sun appears to move across the sky from east to west.

k6l52.q: A ___ is a self-luminous celestial body, such as the Sun.

k6l52.expl: Stars generate and emit their own light, whereas planets and moons shine by reflecting starlight.

chunks: We see the Sun rise in the east
because Earth rotates on its axis

k6l53.q: Why are we able to see the Moon in the night sky even though the Moon is not a star?

Because the Moon is a giant LED bulb

k6l53.q: Approximately how many weeks apart are two consecutive full Moons (Trăng tròn, Question 2 on page 184)?

k6l53.q: What is the difference between No Moon / New Moon (Không Trăng / Trăng non) and Full Moon (Trăng tròn)?

At No Moon, the Moon is square; at Full Moon, it is triangular
There is no difference between them
At Full Moon, the Moon disappears from space

Because the Moon changes its true physical size from 1 cm to 1,000 km every week
Because clouds cover half the Moon on purpose every night
Because sunlight stops reaching the Moon for 20 days

k6l53.q: Why does only one side of the Moon always face Earth according to the "Em có biết?" box on page 186?

Because Earth is attached to the Moon by a steel rod
Because the Moon orbits once every 1 minute
