k7l33.q: What is responsiveness (cảm ứng) in living organisms?
opts: The reaction of an organism to stimuli from the environment
The melting of ice in warm water
The rusting of iron in damp air
The breaking of rocks by wind

a.quiz: The reaction of an organism to stimuli from the environment

k7l33.expl: Responsiveness is the ability of an organism to detect and respond to stimuli from its environment.

k7l33.q: In Figure 33.1, how do plant shoots and plant roots respond to one-sided light and a water source?
opts: Shoots bend toward light; roots grow toward the water source
Shoots grow underground away from light; roots grow up into the air
Neither shoots nor roots respond to light or water

a.quiz: Shoots bend toward light; roots grow toward the water source

k7l33.hint: Look at Figure 33.1a and 33.1b on page 138.
k7l33.expl: Plant shoots bend toward directional light (phototropism), and roots grow toward moisture/water (hydrotropism).

k7l33.q: How does innate behavior (tập tính bẩm sinh) differ from learned behavior (tập tính học được)?
opts: Innate behavior is present from birth and species-specific; learned behavior is acquired during life through learning and experience
Innate behavior is learned in school; learned behavior is present before birth
Only plants have innate behavior; only rocks have learned behavior
There is no difference between them

a.quiz: Innate behavior is present from birth and species-specific; learned behavior is acquired during life through learning and experience

k7l33.expl: Innate behavior is inherited and present from birth, whereas learned behavior is formed during an individual’s life through experience.

k7l33.q: Why do wild buffalo live in herds (sống theo đàn) and swallows migrate south in late autumn?
opts: Herding helps defend against predators; migration helps birds find warmer weather and abundant food
Herding makes buffalo invisible; migration freezes swallows
Both are caused by magnets in soil

a.quiz: Herding helps defend against predators; migration helps birds find warmer weather and abundant food

k7l33.expl: Living in herds protects buffalo from predators and harsh conditions, while seasonal migration brings swallows to warm areas with food.

k7l33.q: How does the cuckoo (chim tu hú, Figure 33.3) reproduce and raise its young?
opts: It lays eggs secretly in another bird’s nest (like a warbler), and the hatched cuckoo chick pushes out host eggs/chicks to get all food
It builds giant mud castles underwater
It feeds only on rocks and sand

a.quiz: It lays eggs secretly in another bird’s nest (like a warbler), and the hatched cuckoo chick pushes out host eggs/chicks to get all food

k7l33.hint: Check the "Em có biết?" story on page 140.
k7l33.expl: The female cuckoo lays look-alike eggs in a host bird’s nest; the early-hatching cuckoo chick ejects host eggs/chicks to monopolize parental feeding.

k7l33.q: ___ is an organism’s reaction to stimuli coming from the environment.

a.quiz: Responsiveness

k7l33.sentence: Responsiveness is a reaction to environmental stimuli.
k7l33.hint: Examples: mimosa leaves folding when touched, chicks running to mother hen.
k7l33.expl: Responsiveness enables organisms to react and adapt to environmental changes.

k7l33.q: ___ behavior is formed during an individual’s lifetime through practice and experience.

a.quiz: Learned

k7l33.hint: Good human habits like sleeping on time are examples.
k7l33.expl: Learned behavior develops through experience and repetition during an individual’s life.

k7l33.q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence.
k7l33.raw: Responsiveness helps organisms adapt to environmental changes in order to survive and develop.
k7l33.sentence: Responsiveness helps organisms adapt to environmental changes in order to survive and develop.
k7l33.expl: This states the role of responsiveness.

k7l33.hint: Three items are animal behaviors in Figure 33.2.
k7l33.expl: Photosynthesis is a plant metabolic process, whereas migration, hunting, and parental care are animal behaviors.

k7l33.q: Human body shivering in cold weather and sweating in hot weather are examples of responsiveness to temperature stimuli.
k7l33.expl: Shivering when cold and sweating when hot are physiological responses to temperature changes.

k7l33.q: Find and correct the mistake: Learned behavior is inherited from birth without experience, whereas innate behavior requires years of schooling.

a.fix: Innate behavior is present from birth without prior learning, whereas learned behavior develops through experience and practice.

k7l33.raw: Innate behavior is present from birth without prior learning, whereas learned behavior develops through experience and practice.
k7l33.hint: Swap innate behavior and learned behavior.
k7l33.expl: Innate behaviors are inborn and species-typical; learned behaviors are acquired through individual experience.

k7l34.q: Why do farmers build trellises or stakes when growing loofah, gourds, pumpkins, or black pepper (Figure 34.1)?
opts: To utilize plant touch responsiveness (thigmotropism) so vines climb upward, receive more sunlight, and yield well
To prevent vines from ever receiving sunlight
To turn vines into underground roots
To keep water away from the soil

a.quiz: To utilize plant touch responsiveness (thigmotropism) so vines climb upward, receive more sunlight, and yield well

k7l34.hint: Check section I and Figure 34.1 on page 141.
k7l34.expl: Climbing plants respond to physical contact by coiling around supports, lifting leaves toward sunlight and improving yield.

k7l34.q: How do light traps (đèn bẫy côn trùng, Figure 34.2b) help protect crops without heavy chemical spraying?
opts: They exploit insects’ attraction to light at night to lure and trap crop-damaging moths and bugs
They freeze insects into solid ice
They make crops grow in complete darkness

a.quiz: They exploit insects’ attraction to light at night to lure and trap crop-damaging moths and bugs

k7l34.hint: Check Table 34.1 and Figure 34.2b on page 142.
k7l34.expl: Many nocturnal insect pests are attracted to light; light traps draw them in and capture them to protect crops.

k7l34.q: What type of behavior allows fish to gather when someone claps hands or cattle to return at the sound of a gong?
opts: Learned behavior conditioned by repeated sound cues paired with feeding or shelter

a.quiz: Learned behavior conditioned by repeated sound cues paired with feeding or shelter

k7l34.hint: Check section II and Figure 34.3 on pages 142–143.
k7l34.expl: Through repeated pairing of a sound cue (clapping, gong, whistle) with food or shelter, animals form a learned response.

k7l34.q: How can students apply learned behavior principles to remember lessons better and build a morning exercise habit?
opts: By reviewing lessons regularly, practicing exercises, and repeating the desired routine consistently
By studying only once a year and staying up late every night
By waiting for innate knowledge without reading

a.quiz: By reviewing lessons regularly, practicing exercises, and repeating the desired routine consistently

k7l34.expl: Learned habits strengthen through consistent repetition and reinforcement, while bad habits are replaced by practicing opposite routines.

k7l34.q: How does the carnivorous pitcher plant (cây nắp ấm, Figure 34.5) capture insects?
opts: It attracts insects with scent from its pitcher-shaped leaves and snaps the lid shut when an insect enters, digesting it for nutrients
It chases insects across the room on legs
It shoots electric sparks at birds
It traps fish underwater with gills

a.quiz: It attracts insects with scent from its pitcher-shaped leaves and snaps the lid shut when an insect enters, digesting it for nutrients

k7l34.hint: Check the "Em có biết?" box on page 144.
k7l34.expl: Pitcher plants secrete attractive nectar/scent; when an insect crawls inside, the lid closes and digestive fluid breaks down the insect for nutrients.

k7l34.q: Farmers set stakes for black pepper vines to use plant ___ responsiveness.

a.quiz: touch

k7l34.hint: Vines coil around supports they touch.
k7l34.expl: Touch responsiveness (thigmotropism) guides climbing stems to coil around poles or trellises.

k7l34.q: Farmers place ___ in rice fields to scare away birds that eat crops.

a.quiz: scarecrows

k7l34.expl: Scarecrows exploit birds’ fear/avoidance response to human-like figures.

k7l34.q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence.
k7l34.raw: Good study and health habits are learned behaviors formed by consistent daily repetition.
k7l34.sentence: Good study and health habits are learned behaviors formed by consistent daily repetition.
k7l34.hint: Start with 'Good study and health habits'.
k7l34.expl: This explains how positive habits are built.

k7l34.hint: Three items are good habits mentioned in section III.

k7l34.q: Training sheepdogs to herd sheep and clapping hands to call fish to feed are practical applications of learned animal behavior.

k7l34.q: Find and correct the mistake: To break the bad habit of waking up late, you should stay up even later and skip setting an alarm.

a.fix: To break the bad habit of waking up late, persistently practice going to sleep on time and waking up early.

k7l34.raw: To break the bad habit of waking up late, persistently practice going to sleep on time and waking up early.
k7l34.expl: Breaking a bad habit requires determination and consistently practicing the opposite positive routine.

k7l35.q: In Experiment 1 (Figure 35.1), how do seedling roots grow in the experimental pot compared with the control pot?
opts: In the experimental pot, roots curve toward the porous water pot; in the control pot, roots grow straight downward
In both pots, roots grow upward out of the soil into the air
Roots disappear completely in the water pot
Roots grow away from water in both pots

k7l35.hint: Look at Figure 35.1a and 35.1b on page 145.
k7l35.expl: In the control pot (even moisture), roots grow straight down; in the test pot, roots curve toward the water source (hydrotropism).

k7l35.q: Why must the small water pot in Experiment 1 have tiny holes that let water seep slowly rather than flooding the entire planter (Question 1 on page 147)?
opts: So water creates a localized moist zone on one side; if the whole pot floods evenly, roots have no directional moisture difference to grow toward
To keep the soil completely dry forever
To turn soil into solid concrete

k7l35.q: In Experiment 2 (Figure 35.2), what happens to bean seedlings covered by the box with a hole on the side?
opts: The stems bend and grow toward the side hole where light enters
The stems bend away from the light into the dark corner
The stems grow downward into the soil

k7l35.q: What happens in the phototropism experiment if you rotate the plant pot frequently in different directions (Question 2 on page 147)?
opts: The stem grows straight upward because all sides receive light evenly over time
The stem ties itself into a knot
The roots grow out of the top hole

k7l35.q: Why should loose, humus-rich soil be chosen when setting up the root hydrotropism experiment (section II.1)?
opts: So seedlings can be gently lifted out after 3–5 days without breaking their delicate roots
Because humus turns roots into glass
So water cannot enter the soil

k7l36.q: How do growth (sinh trưởng) and development (phát triển) differ in definition?
opts: Growth is an increase in body size and mass; development includes growth, cell differentiation, and organ/body morphogenesis
Growth only happens in dead wood; development only happens in rocks
Growth and development never occur in the same organism
Development means shrinking to zero size

a.quiz: Growth is an increase in body size and mass; development includes growth, cell differentiation, and organ/body morphogenesis

k7l36.expl: Growth refers to quantitative increases in size/mass via cell division and enlargement, while development encompasses growth, differentiation, and morphogenesis.

k7l36.q: What is the relationship between growth and development in an organism’s life cycle?
opts: They are closely intertwined: development relies on growth, and without growth there is no development and vice versa
Development happens 100 years before growth starts
Only animals grow and only plants develop

a.quiz: They are closely intertwined: development relies on growth, and without growth there is no development and vice versa

k7l36.expl: Growth and development alternate and depend on each other throughout the life cycle.

k7l36.q: Where is the apical meristem (mô phân sinh đỉnh) located, and what is its function?
opts: At root tips and shoot buds (apical and axillary buds); it lengthens stems, branches, and roots
Only inside dry seeds; it stops all growth
In the center of animal hearts; it pumps blood
Only on fallen dead leaves; it turns them into soil

a.quiz: At root tips and shoot buds (apical and axillary buds); it lengthens stems, branches, and roots

k7l36.hint: Check section II and Figure 36.2 on page 149.
k7l36.expl: Apical meristems at root tips and shoot buds divide to increase the length of roots, stems, and branches.

k7l36.q: What is the function of the lateral meristem (mô phân sinh bên) in dicot stems and roots?
opts: It increases the diameter/thickness (width) of stems, branches, and roots

k7l36.hint: Check Figure 36.2 and Table 36.1 on pages 149–150.
k7l36.expl: Lateral meristem increases girth/thickness (horizontal growth) in dicot stems, branches, and roots.

k7l36.q: How do monocot plants such as bamboo (tre) grow tall quickly despite lacking lateral meristem?
opts: They have intercalary meristems (mô phân sinh lóng) at stem nodes that elongate internodes rapidly
They have iron bones inside their stems
They grow only from underground rocks

a.quiz: They have intercalary meristems (mô phân sinh lóng) at stem nodes that elongate internodes rapidly

k7l36.hint: Check Figure 36.3 and the "Em có biết?" box on page 150.
k7l36.expl: Monocots possess intercalary meristems at stem nodes (mắt thân) that rapidly lengthen internodes (lóng).

k7l36.q: ___ is the increase in body size and mass resulting from increases in cell number and cell size.

k7l36.hint: Quantitative increase in size and weight.
k7l36.expl: Growth occurs when cells divide and enlarge, increasing the organism’s size and mass.

k7l36.q: ___ meristems at root tips and shoot buds help stems, branches, and roots grow longer.

k7l36.hint: Located at the tips/apices of shoots and roots.
k7l36.expl: Apical meristems drive lengthwise elongation at root tips and buds.

k7l36.hint: Three items are types of plant meristems in Lesson 36.
k7l36.expl: A pulmonary vein is a human blood vessel, whereas apical meristem, lateral meristem, and intercalary meristem are plant meristems.

k7l36.q: In an orange tree’s life cycle (Figure 36.1a), stages include seed, germinating seed, seedling, mature tree, and flowering/fruiting.

k7l36.q: Find and correct the mistake: Lateral meristem makes roots and shoots grow longer, while apical meristem makes the trunk wider.

k7l37.q: In Figure 37.1, what are the optimum temperature, favorable range, and lethal limits for tilapia fish?

Optimum: 5.6°C; Favorable range: 0°C–10°C; Lethal limits: 30°C and 100°C
Optimum: 42°C; Favorable range: 40°C–60°C; Lethal limits: -10°C and 5°C
Temperature has no effect on tilapia growth

k7l37.hint: Read the labels on the graph in Figure 37.1 on page 151.
k7l37.expl: Tilapia grows best at 30°C (favorable range 23°C–37°C) and dies below 5.6°C or above 42°C.

k7l37.q: How does morning or late-afternoon sunlight benefit young children and basking animals?

Sunlight turns skin into leaves for photosynthesis
Sunlight removes all calcium from bones

k7l37.hint: Check Figure 37.4c and Table 37.1 on page 154.
k7l37.expl: Growth inhibitors suppress bud sprouting in stored bulbs and tubers such as onions, garlic, and potatoes.

k7l37.q: Why do foresters plant timber trees densely when young and thin them out after they reach the desired height (Question 2 on page 153)?
opts: Dense planting encourages young trees to grow tall and straight upward for light; thinning later gives space to grow thicker trunks
Trees grow downward if planted densely

k7l37.hint: Think about competition for overhead light vs. trunk thickening.
k7l37.expl: Early crowding stimulates upward height growth with straight trunks; later thinning increases light and space so lateral meristems thicken the wood.

k7l37.q: At which life-cycle stage is mosquito control most effective, and why (Figure 37.5a)?
opts: At the egg and aquatic larva/pupa stages by removing stagnant water, because they are concentrated in water and cannot fly away
Only after adult mosquitoes have bitten thousands of people
During winter hibernation in outer space

k7l37.hint: Check section II.3 and Figure 37.5a on pages 154–155.
k7l37.expl: Mosquito larvae and pupae live confined in stagnant water, making draining standing water the easiest and most effective way to break their life cycle.

k7l37.q: Sunlight helps animals and humans synthesize vitamin ___ to absorb calcium for bone growth.

k7l37.expl: Sunlight triggers vitamin D synthesis, which supports calcium absorption and skeletal growth.

k7l37.q: To prevent stored garlic and potatoes from sprouting, farmers apply a growth ___.

k7l39.q: What defines asexual reproduction (sinh sản vô tính)?
opts: Reproduction without fusion of male and female gametes, where offspring develop from part of one parent

Growth of a single leaf without forming a new plant
Pollination by wind between two flowers

Sweet potato: flower; Bryophyllum: seed; Strawberry: pollen

All three reproduce by animal eggs

Hydra: seeds; Starfish: spores; Honeybee drones: stem cutting
All three reproduce only by binary fission

Because leaves grow only from dry bark without buds

k7l39.q: Which propagation method is most effective for rapidly restoring rare, endangered, or disease-free plants (e.g., Ngoc Linh ginseng, orchids)?

Cutting off all roots and discarding the plant

k7l39.q: Find and correct the mistake: Asexual reproduction requires fusion of sperm and egg and produces offspring completely different from the parent.

k7l40.q: What is the essential difference between sexual reproduction and asexual reproduction?
opts: Sexual reproduction involves fusion of male and female gametes to form a zygote and produces diverse offspring; asexual reproduction does not
Sexual reproduction occurs only in bacteria without gametes
Asexual reproduction always requires flowers and bees
Sexual reproduction produces identical clones with zero variation

k7l40.q: Which flowers in Figure 40.2 are unisexual flowers (hoa đơn tính) versus bisexual flowers (hoa lưỡng tính)?

k7l40.q: After fertilization in a flowering plant, which flower parts develop into the seed and the fruit (Figure 40.3)?

Rabbits lay eggs in water; frogs give birth to live young
Chickens have external fertilization in rivers

k7l40.q: Why is internal gestation and live birth (mang thai và sinh con) in mammals advantageous over egg-laying (Question 3 on page 167)?

Mammal embryos never need nutrients or oxygen
Live-bearing animals cannot move or care for young

k7l40.q: In flowering plants, the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma is called ___.

k7l41.q: Why do farmers light dragon fruit orchards at night during winter (Figure 41.1)?

k7l41.q: Why is it important to protect pollinating insects such as honeybees and wasps (Figure 41.3)?

Because they prevent plants from ever flowering
Because they turn seeds into stones
